item.title: Europa League: Bournemouth Hammer 10-Man Milan, Juventus Denied At The Death
item.description: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe’s leading clubs. Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered. Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week. Bournemouth’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace were held 2-2 by Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo. AC Milan’s Italian defender #33 Davide Bartesaghi reacts after the UEFA Europa League, league stage football match between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium in Bournemouth, southern England on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games. Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Rennes’ French goalkeeper #30 Brice Samba speaks with Juventus’ German forward #27 Nick Woltemade at the end of the UEFA Europa League – 1st round day 3 football match between Juventus and Rennes at the Allianz stadium in Turin, on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. The Blacks Cats took a second minute leadin Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win. With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ side. Marseille went down 1-0 to Sturn Graz while Lyon suffered a 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Hoffenheim. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ house burgled while playing for Man Utd in Champions League
item.description: Manchester United are offering full support to Bruno Fernandes and his family after a burglary at his home while he was playing in a Champions league clash against Como on Wednesday evening. A damaging evening in Lombardy saw United fall to a heavy 4-1 defeat against Cesc Fabregas’ side, lengthening their winless streak to seven matches and prompting Fernandes to openly criticise the tactics of boss Michael Carrick . Having flown back from Italy alongside his teammates early on Thursday morning, the Portuguese international was forced to handle the fallout from the break-in that occurred during his time abroad. It is understood that Fernandes’ family were not present when the incident occurred, with officers attending promptly and United giving full assistance to their skipper. Fernandes, meanwhile, is set to escape internal punishment after the Manchester United captain’s outburst in Como. The defeat and Fernandes' statements intensified scrutiny over Carrick’s position prior to Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth, but it is understood he will remain in his post . United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season’s performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick’s tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week’s remarks by Lisandro Martinez. Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics after the Como defeat (PA) Fernandes claimed it was the staff’s decision “not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind” in Como. Captain Fernandes, who was substituted after 67 minutes at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, delivered a damning assessment after the game. He told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind, and trying to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. “Sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work.” Asked further about the tactics, he said: “It’s on the manager and on the staff to say it, it is not on me. “I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable, as they did to us.” Yet, the Press Association understands United are not expected to punish Fernandes for his impassioned post-match interview a week on from Martinez’s caustic remarks, which led to a fine and talks with the club hierarchy.

item.title: Clark girls water polo set to take on Hebron in first state tournament appearance
item.description: Clark's Colette Dreher (right) looks to throw during the UIL water polo regionals against Harlan on Oct. 17, 2026. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) After watching her older sister pick up club water polo, Colette Dreher decided to follow in her sibling's footseteps. Now, Dreher has reached a level of competition her sister, Lilly, a former Clark water polo team captain, dreamt of - the state tournament. "This has been years in the making," she said Thursday morning. Clark girls water polo is making its first UIL state tournament appearance in program history this Friday. Clark (26-3) faces Lewisville Hebron (26-0) in a 10 a.m. state semifinal match at Josh Davis Natatorium. The winner plays Clute Brazoswood or Richmond Foster in Saturday morning's state title match. "There's a lot of nerves, especially because it's gonna be a really big game," freshman defender Maddie Halliburton said. "But I'm actually just really excited that we got all this far." In the boys tournament, Boerne Champion is representing the Greater San Antonio area. Boerne Champion (25-3) faces League City Clear Creek (32-3-1) at 1:30 p.m. Friday afternoon in the state semifinals. The winner plays Austin Westlake or Hebron in the boys state finals at noon Saturday. Boerne Champion's boys team has qualified for the state tournament for five straight seasons. MORE HS SPORTS: UIL approves girls flag football pilot program to begin in 2028-29 Clark's match against Hebron on Friday will be the second time Clark takes on the Hawks this season. The two teams faced off in a mid-August tournament that resulted in a 11-4 Hebron victory. "We were just trying to get the groove of everything," junior Ali Maldonado said of the early season match against Hebron. "I think this time is going to be a lot different than before. We were all trying to figure out who we were as players and trying to figure out the team and trying to figure out each other." But at this point in the season, Clark has the identity it was working to develop in August. "We have a lot more chemistry now," Clark assistant coach Rebecca Halliburton said. "We're really playing to our strengths. We know what they have. We know this is not going to be an easy battle, but we're prepared." Dreher usually keys in on the other team's top defenders to allow Maldonado and Halliburton to operate on offense. "It's my job as the third component to be the defender on their best player," Dreher said. "Just kind of stick to them the whole game." The trio has been critical to Clark's success so far this season. Statistically, Maldonado leads the team in scoring with 113 goals and Dreher is the team's assists leader with 54. Clark's Alicia Maldonado looks to throw during the UIL water polo regionals against Harlan on Oct. 17, 2026. The trio has been critical to Clark's success so far this season. Statistically, Maldonado leads the team in scoring with 113 goals and Dreher is the team's assists leader with 54. Clark's Alicia Maldonado looks to throw during the UIL water polo regionals against Harlan on Oct. 17, 2026. (Blaine Young/For the Express-News) When Clark took down Harlan 14-13 in the regional final last weekend to qualify for state, Halliburton scored a team-high seven goals, including the game winner. She also leads the team in steals with 116 this season. "We have such good chemistry," Maldonado said. "And I think that's why we are such a strong team in the water and outside of the water." Dreher believes surviving the close Harlan match only brought the team closer together. Halliburton's game-winner came at the 2:35 mark in the final period, and the Clark defense prevented Harlan from taking a final shot as time expired. "That game we didn't let it slip, and if anything, we let it bring us closer together," Dreher said. "I think that does make us more confident for the Hebron game." While Clark will have to go through a familiar opponent to become the first San Antonio area girls water polo team to win a UIL championship, the Cougars' belief in each other has already led them to make school history. "It's always been a thought in the back of our mind," Maldonado said of making state. "But we just knew that we had to just go game by game, and we knew that we could make it this far." Clark's Colette Dreher (right) looks to block a throw during the UIL water polo regionals against Harlan on Oct. 17, 2026. item.title: Sarri: ‘Atalanta more positive than negative, unexpected defeat to Ajax’
item.description: Sarri: ‘Atalanta more positive than negative, unexpected defeat to Ajax’ Maurizio Sarri sees ‘more positives than negatives’ from Atalanta’s 2-0 Conference League loss to Ajax . ‘Going into the last five minutes, the last thing I was thinking about was defeat.’ La Dea had some good scoring opportunities and a decent amount of possession in Amsterdam, but were ultimately undone by two late errors. The first saw youth academy product Relja Obric muscled off a long ball by Tolu Arodokare, then Abdella Ouazane blasted in off the underside of the bar from the tightest of angles for the 2-0 result. Sarri irritated with Atalanta defeat AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Michel, Head Coach of Ajax, a Maurizio Sarri, Head Coach of Atalanta BC, before the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff Arena on October 22, 2026 in Amsterdam, Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) “We made a mistake and it cost us a goal, but it’s not as if we can blame the lads too much for that,” Sarri told Sky Sport Italia. “The second half we were under pressure, but managed to create numerous chances on the counter, but we failed to make the most of those situations. It was a performance of tempo and intensity, worthy of the European level against a good team. “Going into the last five minutes, the last thing I was thinking about was a defeat, because the situation seemed to be favourable for us. I am sorry for our fans, so many came here to see us.” It was the second senior game for Obric, who also made a costly error in his senior debut at the weekend in a 3-2 Serie A defeat to Milan. This has been a baptism of fire for the youngster, who was forced to play due to a growing injury crisis in defence. AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Players of Atalanta BC pose for a team photograph before the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff Arena on October 22, 2026 in Amsterdam, Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) “We need a result to get out of this, but we mustn’t leave the stadium tonight feeling distraught,” insisted Sarri. “A little angry, maybe frustrated, but not distraught, because it was a strong performance, we showed improvement in some areas, and there are more positives than negatives to take from this game.” Atalanta were swarming around Ajax on several occasions, but didn’t manage to finish off the move or even truly test Marc-Andre ter Stegen. “I agree, at this level you cannot have three on two and not even get a shot on target. I also want to note we should not have left Obric alone against an opponent who is taller and stronger, there should’ve been help from his teammates.” AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS – OCTOBER 22: Eljif Elmas of Atalanta BC shoots under pressure from Youri Baas of Ajax during the UEFA Conference League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Ajax and Atalanta BC at Johan Cruijff

(Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) So far this season, Atalanta have conceded many goals, but are nowhere near as effective going forward as one would expect either from this club, or from a Sarri side. “I believe we can improve defensively too. I never mentioned the absences, but we were without four central defenders tonight, and that is a lot. If there is a responsibility for the defeat today, I would put it less at the feet of the defence, and more at the failure to take the scoring opportunities,” concluded Sarri.

item.title: Jason Wilcox vs. Christopher Vivell: Tensions rising between Man United chiefs over major decision
item.description: Jason Wilcox vs. Christopher Vivell: Tensions rising between Man United chiefs over major decision Manchester United executives Jason Wilcox and Christopher Vivell are reportedly at odds with each other over a major club decision. Turmoil United are once again in a turbulent state amidst their woeful start to the season. After a poor summer window in which several areas were overlooked, United are enduring a dreadful run of form that has seen them go seven games without a victory. The Red Devils have registered just two wins across all competitions this term: against Ipswich Town in the Premier League and Sabah FK in the Champions League. They were knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the first time of asking by Brighton & Hove Albion. United stooped to a new all-time low on Wednesday as they were beaten 4-1 by Como in the Champions League. Following this latest disappointing result, Michael Carrick finds himself in a highly precarious position, with his departure seemingly only a matter of time. After the final whistle, Carrick blamed his players for not working hard enough, while skipper Bruno Fernandes aimed a dig at the manager’s tactics. A recent report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that members of the United hierarchy were left shocked by the team’s woeful performance in Italy. Carrick will take charge of Sunday’s meeting against Bournemouth but links to his potential replacements are gathering pace, with the likes of Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler and Julian Nagelsmann being lined up. According to the Daily Mail , there are growing tensions between Wilcox and Vivell regarding the choice of manager to replace Carrick. Rift emerging The newspaper claims, “Manchester United’s problems are piling up with there understood to be growing tensions between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell.” “Speaking to a handful of key figures close to the dressing room, each of whom are in regular dialogue with the United hierarchy, Daily Mail Sport has learned that along with disagreements on the pitch between players and manager, there is also growing discontent in the boardroom.” “Wilcox and Vivell are said to have differing opinions on who should succeed Michael Carrick, should the decision be made to move on to a third manager in 2026.” It is understood that Vivell is pushing hard for Nagelsmann, while Wilcox is championing the appointment of a Premier League-tested coach such as Howe or Hurzeler. Nathan Salt explains that there is a degree of sympathy for Carrick, owing to a feeling that the players have let him down with their performances and lack of application. Carrick will speak to the media on Friday in his pre-match press conference for the Bournemouth meeting.

After the final whistle, Carrick blamed his players for not working hard enough, while skipper Bruno Fernandes aimed a dig at the manager’s tactics. A recent report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that members of the United hierarchy were left shocked by the team’s woeful performance in Italy. Carrick will take charge of Sunday’s meeting against Bournemouth but links to his potential replacements are gathering pace, with the likes of Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler and Julian Nagelsmann being lined up. According to the Daily Mail , there are growing tensions between Wilcox and Vivell regarding the choice of manager to replace Carrick. Rift emerging The newspaper claims, “Manchester United’s problems are piling up with there understood to be growing tensions between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell.” “Speaking to a handful of key figures close to the dressing room, each of whom are in regular dialogue with the United hierarchy, Daily Mail Sport has learned that along with disagreements on the pitch between players and manager, there is also growing discontent in the boardroom.” “Wilcox and Vivell are said to have differing opinions on who should succeed Michael Carrick, should the decision be made to move on to a third manager in 2026.” It is understood that Vivell is pushing hard for Nagelsmann, while Wilcox is championing the appointment of a Premier League-tested coach such as Howe or Hurzeler. Nathan Salt explains that there is a degree of sympathy for Carrick, owing to a feeling that the players have let him down with their performances and lack of application. Carrick will speak to the media on Friday in his pre-match press conference for the Bournemouth meeting.

item.title: 3 best Saquon Barkley trade destinations if Eagles’ fire sale continues

Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The idea of the Philadelphia Eagles having a fire sale at the trade deadline is starting to gain momentum. Philly was already falling apart before Week 6, but the Jalen Hurts blood clot fiasco could be the final nail in the team’s coffin. Now the Eagles have a depleted offensive line, no starting quarterback, and an offense that is stuck in the mud. A midseason comeback just does not look realistic for this team. If the Eagles do have a fire sale, aging veterans like Saquon Barkley could be tempting trade targets for other teams. “Barkley and Baun fit this category. Both players are in their age-29 seasons,” The Athletic’s Zach Berman wrote on Tuesday. “They presumably have fewer prime years ahead of them than behind them and would fetch valuable NFL Draft resources. But if they’re slated to help the Eagles compete in 2027, Roseman would be less inclined to listen.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Barkley is widely expected to return to practice on Thursday , giving him a chance to play on Monday Night Football in Week 7. This is great news, as Barkley’s return could help other teams feel comfortable putting in a trade call for him. Should Philly actually consider moving Saquon at the deadline? And if so, which teams make the most sense to trade him to? Here three of the best trade destinations for Barkley if the Eagles do end up having a fire sale at the deadline. Would the Texans immediately become AFC South favorites by adding Saquon Barkley? Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Houston as a landing spot just makes too much sense. The David Montgomery trade has not worked out for the Texans. Woody Marks has been solid, but he is more of a rotational running back than a true three-down starter. Would the Texans immediately become AFC South favorites by adding Saquon Barkley? Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Houston as a landing spot just makes too much sense. The David Montgomery trade has not worked out for the Texans. Woody Marks has been solid, but he is more of a rotational running back than a true three-down starter. Houston invested a lot in their offensive line this offseason to improve the running game. That unit does deserve some blame for how the offense has struggled so far this season. However, they’re good enough to open up running lanes wide enough for Barkley to create some magic. The Texans just proved they’re willing to improve their offense by bringing in Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals. Adding Barkley on top of the team’s existing stars could make Houston’s offense truly dangerous. One big concern is whether or not Houston has the stomach to make another big in-season trade this year. If the Eagles demand a premium for Saquon, then the Texans may not have the capital to get a trade done. Still, this is the most obvious landing spot on paper strictly in terms of need. The Vikings could supercharge their offense by adding a star like Saquon Kevin O’Connell loves to run the football in Minnesota. Imagine how good his offense would look with Barkley pounding the rock. Minnesota has mostly relied on an aging Aaron Jones throughout much of the 2026 season. Jordan Mason is set to return in Week 7 , which should help matters. But the Vikings may want to consider going all in on this season after surprisingly starting the season a perfect 5-0. One big factor here is how incredible the Vikings have looked on defense this year. It is not farfetched to imagine Minnesota becoming a Super Bowl contender if they can add one final piece to their offense. If the Eagles will accept a third-round pick for Barkley (the one gained in the Jonathan Greenard trade? ), then the Vikings need to seriously consider pulling the trigger. Saquon Barkley would give the Broncos a legitimate workhorse running back David Gonzales-Imagn Images This may be the most exciting option of the three. During the Sean Payton era in Denver, the offense has always felt like they are one superstar away from becoming unstoppable. Some may have thought the Jaylen Waddle trade was that move, but he has yet to impress while on the Broncos. If the Broncos did acquire Barkley, it could completely open up the offense. Denver already has a decent stable of running backs with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey sharing carries. But imagine how good those back could be as situational options behind a superstar like Barkley. Honestly, that feels more appropriate for both players instead of being a starting tandem. Barkley’s ability to thrive in the receiving game, and rip off big runs on the ground, make him a threat on every play. It is easy to imagine Payton coming up with some creative ways to get Barkley the ball. He could also use Barkley as a decoy at times to create mismatches for other players on the offense. Denver is projected to have extra picks in the 2027 NFL Draft between the Devaughn Vele trade and a potential comp pick for John Franklin-Myers. Perhaps they use some of that extra draft capital to bring in a star who could change the entire offense. The Broncos will need all the help they can get to get back to the AFC Championship this year. Adding Barkley could help them get one step further and finally make it back to the Super Bowl. item.title: Rays Not Starting Drew Rasmussen In Game 1 of World Series
item.description: Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Drew Rasmussen The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers will play Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, and it will be Jacob Misiorowski facing off against Nick Martinez. The Rays are opting to start Nick Martinez, giving Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta an extra day of rest. Rasmussen will be on five days of rest if he starts Game 2, and Peralta will be on six days of rest after making two starts and a relief outing in the American League Division Series. Martinez has faced the Brewers once this season and gave up four hits, including one double and one home run. Of the Rays' top three starters, the Brewers' group of position players expected to be on the World Series roster have the most success against Martinez. The Brewers' 13 position players have combined to go 30-for-122 with a .737 OPS against Martinez in his career. They also have six home runs and four walks. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Martinez had a 3.10 ERA in 31 starts this year after a down year with the Cincinnati Reds last year. He has made two postseason starts, posting a 3.00 ERA. Against the New York Yankees, he did not make it through four innings. The Rays will be looking for him to be sharp against Misiorowski, but this move allows them to get Rasmussen and Peralta at their best. If Rasmussen pitches in Game 2, he will be lined up on five days of rest for Game 6. Assuming Peralta gets the ball in Game 3, he would be on four days of rest for what would be an all-hands-on-deck Game 7. More MLB: World Series Champion Catcher Retires After 10 MLB Seasons

item.title: Bournemouth stun 10-man AC Milan to claim famous win in Europa League
item.description: Bournemouth's Amine Adli (C) celebrates scoring his side's third goal with teammates during the UEFA Europa League soccer match between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium. (is associated with: «Bournemouth stun 10-man AC Milan to claim famous win in Europa League») Andrew Matthews/PA Wire/dpa Bournemouth scaled giddy new heights in their debut Europa League campaign as 10-man AC Milan were convincingly brushed aside 3-0 at the Vitality Stadium. The Italian giants, champions of Serie A only four years ago, were wretched, unable to match Marco Rose’s team who pressed them ruthlessly and attacked breathlessly in torrential conditions on the south coast. The first two goals were penalties scored in the first half, by Justin Kluivert then by Marcus Tavernier, before Amine Adli added a magnificent late free-kick, but the home side ought to have had even more to show for their dominance. Mike Maignan, the Milan goalkeeper and captain, let his team and his manager Ruben Amorim down badly and inexplicably, swiping at the face of James Hill at a corner, conceding a spot-kick and leaving his side to play for more than an hour with 10 players. Bournemouth have looked perfectly at home on their maiden European adventure but, even so, this fixture had an almost surreal sound to it, the seven-time champions of Europe taking a hammering on a pitch that was hosting League Two football as recently as 2010. “How did we end up here?” read a huge tifo unfurled in the North Stand before kick-off, but Bournemouth’s display suggested this might be just the beginning for them in Europe.

item.title: Did Colin Cowherd just reveal the underlying truth about Texas HC Steve Sarkisian’s coaching of Arch Manning?
item.description: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Did Colin Cowherd just reveal the underlying truth about Texas HC Steve Sarkisian’s coaching of Arch Manning? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Colin Cowherd had some insight to provide into the Texas Longhorns’ situation between Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning midway through the 2026 season. Texas got off to a promising start, winning its first four games and rising to No. 1 of the AP Top 25. They have since lost two consecutive games against Oklahoma and Florida in collapsing fashion, free falling down to 19th in the latest rankings. Cowherd did an episode of The Herd on Thursday, giving his stance into the situation. He believes the Manning family name is placing pressure on Sarkisian to not mess up Arch’s trajectory as a prospective professional player in the NFL. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There is pressure to not screw up Arch Manning … I honestly think [Sark] is trying to protect his NFL career,” Cowherd said. “Arch should be running. It should be Tebow-esque. Texas should be running the ball 60 to 65 percent of the time. A total college offense leaning into Arch’s size and athletic ability, but if you do that, that’s not the NFL. Are you screwing with his NFL career? And I think Sark almost subliminally is not running the offense that is best for Arch. He’s building a pro-style offense, and that’s not really playing to his strengths.” "There is pressure to not screw up Arch Manning… I honestly think [Sark] is trying to protect his NFL career." @colincowherd doesn't think Sark is setting Arch up for success at Texas pic.twitter.com/5qyKPIt5f0 — Herd w/Colin Cowherd (@TheHerd) October 22, 2026 What lies ahead for Steve Sarkisian, Texas Texas still has a chance to get its campaign back on track to be in the CFP mix. However, another loss would their hopes for the tournament and put an end to the dynamic between Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Texas has a 4-2 overall record this season, going 1-2 in its SEC contests so far. They sit at 12th place in the conference standings, being above the Texas A&M Aggies and the South Carolina Gamecocks while trailing the Oklahoma Sooners and the Auburn Tigers. The No. 19 Longhorns will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels in Week 8 as kickoff commences on Oct. 24 at 7:30 p.m. ET. Related: Celebration Bowl introduces interesting way to identify HBCU contenders Related: Bills’ Dalton Kincaid will spend bye week in Utah trying to match Steve Young’s perfect College GameDay picks record

item.title: Steelers’ Paris bar fan event’s fate sealed amid protests
item.description: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images. Steelers’ Paris bar fan event’s fate sealed amid protests appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers will no longer hold their planned Steelers House gathering in Paris this weekend after recent protests prompted security concerns around the event’s location. Pittsburgh canceled the fan gathering at a bar in the Bastille neighborhood ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints . The decision affects the team-sponsored event but does not change plans for Sunday’s game at Stade de France. “Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris,” a message sent to fans read, according to The Associated Press. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Steelers described the decision as a precaution after the Bastille area experienced recent disruptions. Additional demonstrations could also take place in Paris and other areas of France over the weekend. The NFL’s broader activities in the city have continued without interruption. Nicki Ewell, the league’s vice president for global events, told the AP that Pittsburgh made the call to cancel Steelers House. The NFL helped distribute the announcement after previously working with the team to promote the gathering. Ewell said other NFL fan events have not been affected. An Irish pub called O’Sullivans in the Bastille area had also advertised a watch party for Sunday’s Steelers-Saints matchup. Roger Goodell addresses security ahead of Steelers’ Paris clash The Steelers reiterated that the league continues to coordinate with local officials as preparations for the game continue. “The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters,” the Steelers said in a statement to the AP. “As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites.” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the unrest Wednesday and expressed confidence that the league has taken the necessary precautions for its Paris game. Goodell said he spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while officials have remained in communication with authorities in Paris and throughout France. “We’ve made all the preparations,” Goodell said. “Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that’s something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made.” The cancellation therefore remains limited to Pittsburgh’s designated Bastille bar event rather than Sunday’s game. The Steelers enter Week 7 at 4-2, while the Saints sit at 2-4. Pittsburgh and New Orleans will meet Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. item.title: PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes
item.description: Demand for new PCs took a hit after months of price hikes, with Counterpoint Research reporting global PC shipments fell 21 percent year-over-year in Q3 2026. That's in line with earlier reports from IDC and Omdia. It's not just PCs, either - that same quarter, smartphone shipments also hit a 14-year low . Counterpoint linked the decline in PC shipments to higher component prices. Up until Q2 2026 , PC shipments had been growing for over two years straight. But over the last several months, RAM, SSDs , and chips from Intel , AMD , and Qualcomm have all gotten more expensive, leading to price hikes on everything from MacBooks to Raspberry Pis . C … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: ESPN catches Steve Kerr spewing Lakers referee conspiracy on hot mic
item.description: Credit: NBA on ESPN As the Golden State Warriors endured a frustrating season-opening loss, head coach Steve Kerr resorted to accusing the referees of giving Luka Dončić and the Los Angeles Lakers a clear home court advantage. With the Warriors trailing the Lakers 81-59 midway through the third quarter Wednesday night, Kerr pulled rookie Yaxel Lendeborg aside to offer the first-round draft pick some words of wisdom during the first game of his young NBA career. The conversation was likely meant to be private, but ESPN mics picked up Kerr’s comments. Steve Kerr CALLED OUT the Lakers whistle on the hot mic: “They call all that sh*t here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena.” https://t.co/FjGzYPdqg9 — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) October 22, 2026 “It’s the bullsh*t in the NBA. They call all that sh*t here, they wouldn’t call it in any other arena,” Kerr told Lendeborg who picked up four fouls in 29 minutes. This coming from the head coach of a team that was widely accused of benefiting from illegal screens to generate open shots for Steph Curry and Klay Thompson during the height of their dynasty. But maybe Kerr never thought the Warriors benefited from those calls in the Lakers’ building. Dončić is often accused of receiving his own whistle advantage by foul-baiting and whining to officials. And Kerr appears to think it worked to the Lakers’ advantage Wednesday night, despite each team visiting the line 27 times. Lendeborg did receive a technical foul for trash talking with Dončić in the first half that probably wasn’t warranted. And after the game, Kerr’s words appeared to resonate with Lendeborg. Because while it may not have been the head coach’s intent, Lendeborg went off during his postgame press conference, claiming he lost all respect for Dončić after witnessing his whining and complaining firsthand. Kerr similarly defended Lendeborg in his own press conference, claiming the rookie was called for at least three fouls that would not have been called in any other league. But the Lakers got the last laugh, blowing out the Warriors 127-105 behind 28 points from Dončić. It’s hard to imagine the referees could have done much to overturn a 22-point blowout loss for Golden State, regardless of where the game was played. The post ESPN catches Steve Kerr spewing Lakers referee conspiracy on hot mic appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama: Five things to watch against the Tide
item.description: Texas A&M football is seeking its first road win over Alabama since 2012 , as the Aggies travel to Tuscaloosa to take on the Crimson Tide on Saturday. It has been 328 days since Mike Elko's squad recorded a touchdown against a ranked opponent, dating back to the Lone Star Showdown against the Texas Longhorns last year. That is something the Aggies are looking to change against the 13th-ranked Tide in Bryant-Denny Stadium in Week 8. Texas A&M is coming off its second shutout of the season, a 41-0 rout of The Citadel, while Alabama suffered a 26-10 upset loss to Tennessee last week. If Elko and company want to dethrone the Crimson Tide, they will need sharp quarterback play and to set the tone in the trenches. Here are five things to watch in Texas A&M's road showdown against Alabama on Saturday: How will Marcel Reed handle the intimidating road environment? The junior from Nashville, Tennessee, enters Saturday's contest against the Crimson Tide as Texas A&M's starting quarterback with a 5-5 road record. In those games, Reed has thrown 10 interceptions, averaging one per road game. This season, he has thrown three interceptions in the Aggies' road losses to LSU and Missouri. Texas A&M can't afford for Reed's inconsistencies to continue against an Alabama defense that has forced 10 interceptions through the first seven weeks. While the Tide are allowing 230.9 passing yards per contest, Reed could be without his star wide receiver Mario Craver, who was listed as "questionable" for the second week in a row in the initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report . Can Texas A&M's defensive line make Keelon Russell feel the heat? Tennessee lived in the backfield in last week's win over Alabama. The Vols recorded five sacks and forced two interceptions from Russell, punishing the Tide's offensive line. To keep a dangerous dual-threat quarterback like Russell from creating explosive plays, the Aggies must find ways to apply pressure, something Mike Elko's defensive unit has struggled to do in 2026. Texas A&M ranks at the bottom of the conference with just 5.0 sacks, averaging less than 1.0 sack per game. Defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill's group is also battling injuries, with starting defensive tackle DJ Hicks and EDGE Anto Saka listed as "questionable" against the Crimson Tide. Can the Aggie wideouts spark offensive success against Alabama's secondary? Despite Craver's status for Saturday's showdown, Texas A&M's offense has some young wide receivers emerging in recent weeks. Sophomore TK Norman and freshman Aaron Gregory combined for 182 yards and two touchdowns in the 41-0 shutout of The Citadel last week, showcasing their ability to stretch the field and create space using their speed. Alabama's secondary has allowed the second-most explosive passing plays in the SEC thus far, which will play an integral role in the Aggies' offensive success. Can Texas A&M's defensive line make Keelon Russell feel the heat? Tennessee lived in the backfield in last week's win over Alabama. The Vols recorded five sacks and forced two interceptions from Russell, punishing the Tide's offensive line. To keep a dangerous dual-threat quarterback like Russell from creating explosive plays, the Aggies must find ways to apply pressure, something Mike Elko's defensive unit has struggled to do in 2026. Texas A&M ranks at the bottom of the conference with just 5.0 sacks, averaging less than 1.0 sack per game. Defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill's group is also battling injuries, with starting defensive tackle DJ Hicks and EDGE Anto Saka listed as "questionable" against the Crimson Tide. Despite Craver's status for Saturday's showdown, Texas A&M's offense has some young wide receivers emerging in recent weeks. Sophomore TK Norman and freshman Aaron Gregory combined for 182 yards and two touchdowns in the 41-0 shutout of The Citadel last week, showcasing their ability to stretch the field and create space using their speed. Alabama's secondary has allowed the second-most explosive passing plays in the SEC thus far, which will play an integral role in the Aggies' offensive success. Will Texas A&M's offensive line establish dominance up front to set up the ground game for success? The Vols dominated the trenches and paved the way for DeSean Bishop to roll for 159 yards and two touchdowns against the Tide's rush defense, which has been excellent for the majority of the 2026 season. Alabama's defense ranks No. 6 in the SEC, allowing just 107.0 rushing yards per contest entering Saturday's matchup against Texas A&M. However, the Aggies have two running backs, true freshman KJ Edwards and senior Rueben Owens II, who have eclipsed 300 rushing yards this season and a third, sophomore Jamarion Morrow, who has recorded 122 yards on the ground and leads the room with four touchdowns, despite missing three games due to injury. If Texas A&M's offensive line can establish dominance in the trenches, like Tennessee, it could open up the playcalling and force Alabama to respect the run. How will the Aggie secondary perform against Russell and Alabama's talented wide receivers? Ryan Coleman-Williams won't play this weekend, but Alabama has other wideouts who can create explosive plays on a dime. That includes sophomore Lotzeir Brooks, who has burst onto the scene and leads the Tide with 415 receiving yards. After a slow start to the 2026 campaign, the Aggies' secondary has consistently improved each week. The unit ranks No. 3 in the league, allowing just 164.1 passing yards per game. The unit must be sharp and prevent talent like Brooks from torching them for big gains. item.title: F1 Today: Hamilton details Singapore GP disaster as Horner speaks out on Red Bull return
item.description: From Lewis Hamilton explaining the costly strategy mistake that compromised his Singapore Grand Prix to Christian Horner ruling out a return to Red Bull more than a year after his dismissal, here are the main Formula 1 stories of the day. Hamilton reveals what went wrong with costly Singapore strategy gamble Lewis Hamilton has explained the circumstances behind his unsuccessful strategy gamble at the Singapore Grand Prix, admitting that he realised his decision to stay out was probably a mistake almost immediately. Speaking to the media ahead of the United States Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion revealed that he wanted to pursue a different strategy from Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, believing that following the same approach would limit his chances of challenging Max Verstappen for victory. However, the gamble backfired. Hamilton struggled on the medium tyres during his opening stint before losing valuable time behind Leclerc. He later decided against entering the pit lane, unaware that his team-mate was coming in, and realised his mistake as he passed the pit entry. The Briton accepted responsibility for the decision but defended his willingness to challenge Ferrari's strategic approach. He also confirmed that discussions have taken place behind the scenes to improve collaboration, insisting that the setback will not discourage him from taking risks in pursuit of better results. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Horner makes Red Bull return stance clear after shock dismissal Christian Horner has ruled out the possibility of returning to Red Bull, bringing an end to speculation about a potential reunion with the team he led for two decades. The Briton was dismissed in July 2025, shortly after the British Grand Prix, ending a remarkable spell that saw Red Bull claim eight Drivers' Championships and six Constructors' Championships. Since his departure, the 52-year-old has been linked with a potential return to Formula 1. Speaking on Jodie Kidd's Kidd in a Sweet Shop YouTube channel, Horner reflected on his time at the Milton Keynes-based outfit, acknowledging that the final years of his tenure were difficult despite the team's considerable success. The former team principal confirmed that he remains on good terms with Red Bull's shareholders but made it clear that his chapter with the Austrian outfit is over. Horner has previously expressed an interest in returning to Formula 1, although only in a role that would allow him to compete for victories. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures

item.title: Jason Kelce praises Chiefs fan for making a Caitlin Clark-style basketball shot
item.description: Source: mkopka/Depositphotots Jason Kelce had a memorable moment with Kansas City Chiefs fans ahead of the team’s Oct. 18, 2026, game against the Los Angeles Chargers. During a pregame tailgate outside Arrowhead Stadium, the retired NFL center watched a fan sink an unusually long basketball shot and immediately connected the moment to WNBA star Caitlin Clark. Kelce, who co-hosts the popular New Heights podcast with his brother, Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, was interacting with fans during the event when the impressive attempt found its mark. The podcast’s official social media account celebrated the moment by referencing Clark’s renowned long-range shooting. The playful comparison brought together two major sports audiences: NFL fans who gathered to support Kansas City and basketball followers familiar with Clark’s ability to make shots from well beyond the three-point line. It also highlighted the growing connection between Clark and the Kelce family. Jason Kelce’s pregame event delivered an unexpected highlight Kelce’s interaction with Chiefs supporters took place during a New Heights tailgate ahead of Kansas City’s matchup with the Chargers. The event gave fans an opportunity to meet the retired Philadelphia Eagles center and participate in activities before kickoff. One basketball challenge produced the afternoon’s standout moment. As a fan prepared to attempt a distant shot, Kelce provided running commentary, building anticipation as the ball traveled toward the basket. The attempt went in, prompting an enthusiastic reaction from Kelce. Rather than treating the successful shot as an ordinary tailgate highlight, he helped turn it into a memorable moment by linking the fan’s range to one of basketball’s most recognizable shooters. The fan’s long-range shot earned a Caitlin Clark comparison Kelce’s commentary included the line, “Here it comes, all the way from New York City,” as the fan launched the ball. The exaggerated description captured the distance involved and added to the excitement surrounding the attempt. After the shot went through the basket, the New Heights account shared the clip with the caption, “From Caitlin Clark range.” The post tagged Clark, making the Indiana Fever star part of the moment even though she was not the person taking the shot. The comparison was a natural fit for Clark’s reputation as an ambitious long-range shooter. Her ability to launch deep 3-pointers has become a defining feature of her game, making her name an easy reference for fans who have seen her connect from far away. Jason Kelce’s pregame event delivered an unexpected highlight Kelce’s interaction with Chiefs supporters took place during a New Heights tailgate ahead of Kansas City’s matchup with the Chargers. After the shot went through the basket, the New Heights account shared the clip with the caption, “From Caitlin Clark range.” The post tagged Clark, making the Indiana Fever star part of the moment even though she was not the person taking the shot. The comparison was a natural fit for Clark’s reputation as an ambitious long-range shooter. Her ability to launch deep 3-pointers has become a defining feature of her game, making her name an easy reference for fans who have seen her connect from far away. Caitlin Clark’s shooting range has become part of her identity Source: ifeelstock/Depositphotos Clark rose to national prominence at the University of Iowa, where her scoring ability and deep shooting helped attract unprecedented attention to women’s college basketball. Her performances made long-range attempts a signature part of her on-court identity. She carried that reputation into the WNBA with the Indiana Fever. Clark’s willingness to shoot from well beyond the conventional 3-point range forces defenders to account for her farther from the basket, creating opportunities for teammates as well as herself. The tailgate comparison was a lighthearted reference, not a claim that the fan’s shot was equivalent to Clark’s performance in a competitive game. Still, it illustrated how recognizable her shooting style has become beyond women’s basketball. Clark’s connection to the Chiefs made the reference even better Clark is not simply a basketball star being mentioned by an NFL personality. She has openly supported the Kansas City Chiefs for years, giving her a genuine connection to the team whose fans attended Kelce’s event. The Iowa native has discussed her Chiefs fandom publicly, and her friendship with the Kelce family has helped bring her into the team’s wider circle. Her appearances alongside Taylor Swift at Chiefs games have also attracted attention. That overlap made the reference especially fitting for a Kansas City tailgate. A basketball shot became an opportunity to recognize a player whose interests extend beyond her own sport and whose connection with the Chiefs is well established. Jason and Travis Kelce have built a relationship with Clark Clark previously appeared on New Heights , where she discussed basketball, her life outside the game and her enthusiasm for the Chiefs. The conversation gave listeners a chance to see her interact with the brothers beyond the usual boundaries of sports coverage. The Kelces have also shown interest in Clark’s career away from the podcast studio. Their public exchanges reflect a friendly relationship that brings together professional football, women’s basketball, and the broader sports-entertainment world. That familiarity helps explain why Clark’s name came naturally into the tailgate moment. The reference was more than a random celebrity comparison; it connected a successful fan shot to a basketball player the Kelce brothers already know. Source: Image Press Agency/Depositphotos The moment highlighted the crossover between football and basketball Professional sports audiences often overlap, particularly when athletes and personalities share interests across leagues. Clark’s Chiefs fandom is one example of how a prominent basketball player can also become part of the conversation surrounding an NFL team. Kelce’s tailgate appearance provided a relaxed setting for that crossover. Fans were not watching a formal competition between professional athletes; they were participating in a pregame gathering where a spontaneous moment could become a highlight. The clip also demonstrated how a short social media post can connect different sports communities. A fan’s long shot, Kelce’s enthusiastic commentary and a reference to Clark combined to make a simple activity more memorable. The New Heights tailgate added to the Chiefs’ game-day atmosphere The New Heights event was part of the buildup to Kansas City’s Oct. 18 home game against the Chargers. Kelce’s presence gave attendees a chance to engage with a familiar football personality before the teams took the field. The tailgate included fan-focused activities and a meet-and-greet opportunity with Jason Kelce. Such gatherings allow supporters to connect with sports figures in a setting that feels more personal than a stadium seat or television broadcast. For Kelce, the basketball challenge offered an unscripted highlight amid the day’s scheduled activities. The fan made the shot, Kelce supplied the excitement, and the podcast account gave the moment a memorable connection to Clark. Clark’s growing influence reaches beyond the basketball court Clark’s impact is evident not only in the attention paid to her games but also in how her name is recognized across sports. Her deep shooting has become a shorthand reference that audiences can understand even outside a basketball arena. Her presence in the Chiefs conversation reflects the same wider appeal. As a prominent Fever player and an established Kansas City supporter, Clark can connect with fans who follow football as closely as they follow basketball. Fun fact: Caitlin Clark’s Chiefs fandom inspired the red “Sea of Red” colorway of her signature Nike Caitlin 1 basketball shoe, which Travis Kelce received as a gift from the WNBA star. TL;DR Jason Kelce praised a Chiefs fan after the supporter made a long-range basketball shot during a pregame tailgate on Oct. 18, 2026. Kelce joked that the ball was coming from New York City as the fan attempted the shot. The New Heights account captioned the clip, “From Caitlin Clark range,” and tagged the Indiana Fever star. Clark is a longtime Chiefs fan and has an established connection with Jason and Travis Kelce. Clark’s first signature Nike shoe, the Caitlin 1, launched on Oct. 1, 2026. item.title: 'Opportunity is great.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian explains why he likes a 24-team CFP
item.description: Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian arrives at the stadium ahead of the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Ask Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian any question about college football, and he'll quickly extol the virtues of his sport. The history, the pomp, the pageantry, the rivalries. Sarkisian admittedly loves it all. But Sarkisian is also pragmatic when it comes to his duties leading the Longhorns. That means he's cautiously optimistic about the impact of the impending 24-team College Football Playoff, which will likely begin next season pending contractual agreements between the SEC, the Big Ten, other collegiate conferences and broadcast partner ESPN. MOR E: How Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, Texas Longhorns grade in midseason report card Texas football head coach Steve Sarkisian said the Longhorns "bled out," in Saturday's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) "Opportunity is great," Sarkisian said Thursday during his weekly Zoom availability with reporters. "More teams get an opportunity to try to win a national championship." Sarkisian then reeled off a few reasons why more teams makes more sense, especially if a squad has to deal with some adversity in an early-season loss that once ended all title hopes. "Maybe you may have had to endure an injury or two," he said. "Maybe your quarterback was out. You get them back, and now you're healthy and you're fresh and you're better. Maybe it gives you an opportunity early in your season to play some younger players, knowing, hey, maybe we have a couple of losses that don't want to lose. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Ask Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian any question about college football, and he'll quickly extol the virtues of his sport. The history, the pomp, the pageantry, the rivalries. Sarkisian admittedly loves it all. But Sarkisian is also pragmatic when it comes to his duties leading the Longhorns. That means he's cautiously optimistic about the impact of the impending 24-team College Football Playoff, which will likely begin next season pending contractual agreements between the SEC, the Big Ten, other collegiate conferences and broadcast partner ESPN. MOR E: How Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, Texas Longhorns grade in midseason report card Texas football head coach Steve Sarkisian said the Longhorns "bled out," in Saturday's 27-24 loss to the Florida Gators. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) "Opportunity is great," Sarkisian said Thursday during his weekly Zoom availability with reporters. "More teams get an opportunity to try to win a national championship." Sarkisian then reeled off a few reasons why more teams makes more sense, especially if a squad has to deal with some adversity in an early-season loss that once ended all title hopes. "Maybe you may have had to endure an injury or two," he said. "Maybe your quarterback was out. You get them back, and now you're healthy and you're fresh and you're better. Maybe it gives you an opportunity early in your season to play some younger players, knowing, hey, maybe we have a couple of losses that don't want to lose. But your team can get better and play your best football at the end of the year with an opportunity to make a run." The expanded CFP eliminates conference title games, so how will the modern conference behemoths - none of the Power Four leagues have less than 16 teams - determine conference championships and automatic playoff berths? Will a selection committee pick every CFP squad as well as its seed? "How are you eligible? How are you not? Is it just the top 24?" Sarkisian asked. "I don't know the specifics of it. I'm a little leery of not having championship games, if that's what comes out of this." Sarkisian does hope more high-profile nonconference games come out of any CFP expansion, since the impact of an early-season loss will no longer eliminate a team from contention. Texas has embraced that type of scheduling under Sarkisian; the Longhorns have played Ohio State and Michigan during Sarkisian's six seasons as coach, and they have a home rematch with Michigan next year as well as a home-and-home schedule with Notre Dame in 2028 and 2029. "What I like most about (expansion), without having really dug into it, honestly, is that we get to keep those nonconference games that I think we all really like," Sarkisian said. "I know we do internally. I know our fans do. I know it's good for college football that we're playing Michigan next year and we've got Notre Dame the next two years after that. item.title: Barcelona want to reinforce one position in January
item.description: Barcelona want to reinforce one position in January La Liga champions Barcelona are expected to seek out fresh blood in one key area of Hansi Flick’s squad with a view to the 2nd half of the campaign. This comes amid the understanding that Deco and co. will set about bringing in a new central defender in January. Barca are of course fresh off seeing their flawless opening to the new campaign brought to an end on Tuesday night. After making the trip to Paris to face European champions PSG, the Blaugrana were condemned to the wrong side of a 4-2 result. En route to defeat, the most glaring weakness in the visitors’ squad was laid bare, as the lack of depth at the heart of Hansi Flick’s backline was badly exposed. In turn, it should come as little surprise to hear of Deco and co. preparing to address this concern in the winter. As per a report from Fichajes : ‘Barcelona have an urgent need to resolve a problem they couldn’t address during the summer. Now, they face the task of signing a defender in the winter transfer window.’ Specifically, the Camp Nou brass are on the lookout for a new left-footed centre-back. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Bears Hit With Sudden Trade Suggestion to Pursue $105.8 Million Star
item.description: The Chicago Bears once again appear to be a serious contender in the NFC. After winning the NFC North division title last year and earning the No. 2 seed in the playoffs, the Bears are currently 4-2 after their Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. Caleb Williams made his return to the field against the Falcons. He completed 30 of his 36 pass attempts for 305 yards, a touchdown, and no interceptions. On paper, Chicago has the necessary talent to be a Super Bowl contender. However, there are still some clear holes the team could look to fill. With the NFL trade deadline coming up on November 10, rumors have started to fly. Ryan Poles has had a very aggressive approach in recent years. Fans should not expect to see that change before the deadline. If the right move presents itself, the Bears will almost certainly pounce. Keeping that in mind, one aggressive suggestion has been made that would see Chicago pursue a blockbuster trade for a $105.8 million star. Aug 26, 2023; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles looks on before a game against the Buffalo Bills at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Bartel-USA TODAY Sports Chicago Bears Named Potential Trade Destination for Jeffery Simmons The Athletic’s Daniel Popper recently created and publsihed a 2026 trade deadline big board. In that column, he suggested Chicago as a trade suitor for Tennessee Titans superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. “Simmons signed a three-year extension in June. The Titans, however, are going nowhere fast under first-year coach Robert Saleh. They earned their first win of the season over the Colts in Week 6. They are nonetheless trending toward another top-five pick, and dealing Simmons would present an opportunity to add valuable draft capital. Simmons is guaranteed $26.95 million in base salary in 2027. He is also due a $5.5 million option bonus in September,” Popper wrote . “Any acquiring team should be comfortable with those figures. Simmons is a game-wrecker as a run defender and pass rusher. Because of the extension, the Titans would take on $21.2 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Simmons.” Simmons is the kind of player who can completely change a defense. So far this season in six games, the 29-year-old has racked up 34 tackles, four sacks, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and three defended passes. Across his entire 105-game NFL career, Simmons has totaled 410 tackles, 46.5 sacks, nine forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries, and 30 defended passes. Whether or not the Bears actually have interest in pursuing a trade for Simmons remains to be seen. Tennessee also has not been reported to be shopping him. But, it’s an idea worth keeping an eye on should the Titans decide to listen to offers. item.title: Top ranked Texas program gets star QB back, but not its three vacated wins
item.description: Lewisville junior quarterback will return to the field on Friday to face Flower Mound. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) One of Texas's best high school quarterbacks has come full circle. On Thursday, the University Interscholastic League (UIL) state executive committee reversed its eligibility ruling on Lewisville junior quarterback Laykon Brassfield . The Fighting Farmers star is now eligible to return to the field after missing four games, but their three vacated wins will not be reinstated. Brassfield's appeal passed by a unanimous vote after the DEC initially voted 7-0 to rule him ineligible after he transferred from Edmond North in Oklahoma to the North Texas school after his sophomore year. The DEC's initial investigation found that Brassfield did not actually reside in Lewisville and declared he could not participate in varsity competition for one calendar year from the date he enrolled at Lewisville. According to UIL executive director Jamey Harrison, the earlier ruling was a "reasonable" at the time What changed in Brassfield's appeal Initial residency questions arose regarding an apartment in Lewisville and a house in Argyle owned by Laykon's grandfather, which was used to enroll his younger siblings in Argyle ISD. Brassfield's father, Jonathan, stated this was to meet the children's educational needs. Attorney Brian Wcislo said the situation was previously disclosed on Lewisville ISD and AISD Athletic Participation Forms. Lewisville's Laykon Brassfield was one of the state's best quarterbacks during the first three weeks of the season. He returns to the field on Friday vs. Flower Mound. (Steve Hamm/The Dallas Morning News) Jonathan Brassfield, Laykon's father, confirmed he was a financial guarantor for the Argyle house while the family lived in a 600-square-foot apartment in Lewisville. They have since moved to a 1,200-square-foot apartment in the Lewisville attendance zone, removed the guarantor status from the Argyle residency, and transferred Laykon's siblings out of Argyle. "I want to reinforce, as a family, we have lived in Lewisville. This has been our home," Jonathan said Thursday. "I certainly hate that there has been confusion in the paperwork that has interrupted my son's life. I take full responsibility for some confusion on the paperwork, but we live in Lewisville; we've lived in Lewisville. We love it here." Lewisville remains "undefeated" without Brassfield Brassfield, named a team captain in his first year with the program, led the Farmers to a 3-0 start and looked like one of the state's best quarterbacks. The Fighting Farmers quarterback threw for 734 passing yards, 14 passing touchdowns and just one interception. On the ground, he added 133 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns. Without their star quarterback, Lewisville has continued to win big, remaining undefeated in district play and outscoring their last four opponents 157-25. item.title: McDermott calls for Super League to accept NRL investment
item.description: Brian McDermott enjoyed a trophy-laden spell as Leeds Rhinos coach between 2011-18 [Getty Images] England head coach Brian McDermott has called for Super League to accept investment from Australia's NRL in order to improve the English game. Talks are currently ongoing after Super League clubs rejected a £35m package from the Australian Rugby League Commission and a second deadline of 15 October was allowed to pass without an agreement being reached. Formalising a partnership between the sport's two leading competitions is seen as as a key step in helping to grow the European competition's revenue. "I think the NRL's investment in Super League could be very, very positive," said McDermott, who is also the assistant coach of the Gold Coast Titans. "The product's brilliant. It has always being brilliant. The product's never been the problem. The players have never been the problem. The coaches have never been the problem. "It's just how it's marketed and how it's presented to people. I think there's some dominoes could start falling our way if the NRL invests and we accept their investment." Super League is yet to agree a new title sponsorship deal, finalise broadcast negotiations or even its fixtures for the 2027 campaign with London Broncos' position yet to be fully determined. The Broncos came in16th on the yearly grading list, below fellow Championship side Barrow Raiders, despite a season in which they won the second tier's Grand Final, the 1895 Cup and were runaway champions in the regular-season standings. The Broncos were overlooked 12 months ago when Bradford Bulls, York Knights and Toulouse Olympique joined the expanded 14-team competition. But with the backing of Australian businessman Grant Wechsel and former Brisbane Broncos star Darren Lockyer, and with a squad full of internationals, they do still harbour hopes of playing in Super League in 2027. It is understood any completed deal would involve the Australian governing body insisting on Broncos featuring in the top flight in the near future. The financial gulf between the northern and southern hemisphere's elite competitions was laid bare, when the NRL struck a record $5.3bn (£3.97bn) television deal over seven years in July. Super League's TV deal with Sky Sports, which expired at the end of 2026, was worth around £21.5m per year. "I know there's some positive notes around Super League at the moment, especially with crowds," McDermott added. "It's been a really interesting competition this year and Wakefield winning the Grand Final puts a brilliant marker down that all the teams can win it. "It would be a real positive validation of Super League if the NRL were to invest." item.title: Max Fried’s elbow news is good, but Yankees still need cover
item.description: 2026 ALDS archive, not the follow-up medical examination. Oct 7, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Max Fried (54) throws during the first inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Max Fried’s follow-up imaging brought the Yankees encouraging news. I would take the relief without allowing it to become the argument against adding another credible starter this winter. Aaron Boone said Fried was recently re-imaged after dealing with a left elbow bone bruise and described the ligament as being in a good place, MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch reported Wednesday . No surgical procedure was scheduled for him in that update. The Yankees got quality, but only 20 starts Fried finished 2026 with a 2.80 ERA, 0.99 WHIP and 104 strikeouts against 33 walks in 112 2/3 innings. Those aren’t the numbers of a pitcher whose ability needs rescuing. He also made 20 starts. The Yankees needed other pitchers to cover the rest of the schedule, and a reassuring October examination can’t guarantee how much work any starter will handle next year. The quality and the workload belong in the same evaluation. 2026 ALDS archive, not the follow-up medical examination. Oct 7, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Max Fried (54) throws during the sixth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game three of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Depth doesn’t require a headline signing I’d want New York to add a pitcher it would be comfortable actually starting, rather than count a collection of emergency options as a finished depth plan. That could come through a modest acquisition or a legitimate internal competition. It doesn’t have to be an expensive name or a trade that creates a different weakness. The practical goal is a sixth starter with a believable path to useful innings. Such a pitcher could cover an absence, make it easier to manage workloads or prevent the club from rushing another arm simply because the schedule needs someone that night. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. There is a sensible case for spending most of the available resources on hitting and trusting younger pitchers to supply the extra starts. That approach becomes more attractive if the internal options show enough to deserve it. I wouldn’t rule it out before seeing the actual cost of an addition. What I wouldn’t accept is substituting good health news for that evaluation. We don’t have the medical records, and this isn’t a prediction that Fried will get hurt again. His 2026 performance supports counting on his talent; his 20-start workload supports preparing for the possibility that the club needs more innings elsewhere. item.title: Tuloso-Midway tennis falls short in state championship, Flour Bluff exits in semis
item.description: Tuloso-Midway’s historic season came to a close Thursday, Oct. 22, after a 10-7 loss to Canyon Randall in the UIL Class 4A tennis state championship. The Warriors reached the championship match for the first time in program history after defeating Fredericksburg 10-5 in the Region IV-4A final and Robinson 10-1 in Wednesday’s state semifinals. Flour Bluff’s season ended Wednesday, Oct. 21, with a dramatic 10-9 loss to Frisco Centennial in the Class 5A state semifinals. The Hornets reached the semifinals for the second consecutive year after defeating Boerne 11-2 in the regional final. Following are the results from Tuloso-Midway's state title matches and Flour Bluff's semifinal matches. item.title: NASCAR Cup Series Preview: Championship Battle Heats Up at Talladega
item.description: Photo by: Jim Dedmon The NASCAR Cup Series heads to Talladega Superspeedway on Sunday for the YellaWood 500, a critical race as the championship Chase enters its final three events. With the title fight tightening, drivers cannot afford a poor finish, and Talladega’s unpredictable nature could dramatically reshape the standings. The 188 lap race is scheduled for 2 p.m. ET on NBC, with drivers preparing for another intense afternoon of superspeedway racing. Kyle Larson Looks to Protect His Championship Lead Kyle Larson enters the weekend leading the championship standings, but his advantage is far from comfortable. Christopher Bell sits just five points behind Larson, while Chase Briscoe, Denny Hamlin, Ryan Blaney and Joey Logano remain within striking distance. Larson needs a clean race after a disappointing result at Phoenix threatened to tighten the championship battle. Talladega presents a different challenge, as drivers must navigate massive drafting packs and avoid the accidents that frequently decide superspeedway races. Bell has an opportunity to take over the championship lead with a strong performance. Briscoe and Hamlin will also be looking to capitalize, knowing that a victory could provide a significant advantage heading into the final two races. Carson Hocevar Hopes to Recreate Talladega Magic Carson Hocevar will be one of the drivers to watch after winning the spring race at Talladega. The Spire Motorsports driver proved he can handle the pressure of a dramatic superspeedway finish, and another victory would further establish him as a serious threat at drafting tracks. Ryan Blaney is another contender. The Team Penske driver has a strong history at Talladega and knows how to position himself near the front when the race reaches its closing laps. Joey Logano, Austin Cindric and Tyler Reddick also have the potential to challenge for the victory. Team Penske’s drafting strength could be particularly important as drivers attempt to maintain momentum through the large packs. Talladega Could Change Everything The 2.66-mile superspeedway is known for close racing, aggressive blocking and last-lap drama. Drivers must balance the need to gain positions with the risk of getting caught in a multi-car accident. Stage points will be important for the championship contenders, but surviving the final laps could ultimately determine their weekend. With Larson’s lead only five points over Bell, every position matters. A victory could completely change the championship picture, while a crash could leave a contender with an enormous deficit. Sunday’s race promises to deliver another unpredictable Talladega showdown as NASCAR’s championship battle approaches its conclusion.

item.title: Amorim: ‘There was no game’ as 10-man Milan punished in Bournemouth
item.description: Amorim: ‘There was no game’ as 10-man Milan punished in Bournemouth Ruben Amorim insists ‘there was no game’ for Milan against Bournemouth, as the going down to 10 men after 28 minutes made it impossible to avoid a 3-0 defeat . ‘We cannot do that.’ The coach famously had a dismal record against Bournemouth on the Manchester United bench, including a 3-0 defeat here, and he continued that trend at the Vitality Stadium. They paid the price for two early naïve errors, the Koni De Winter handball for the opening Justin Kluivert penalty, then Mike Maignan’s shove on Tyler Adams prompting the double whammy of a red card and new penalty, converted by Marcus Tavernier. Amine Adli added a third late on with a free kick, and goal difference could be decisive in this Europa League format. Amorim regret at Milan errors BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, interacts with Mike Maignan after he receives a red card during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) “The penalty on the corner and the red card changed everything, so it was not a game. It was not a game,” Amorim told Sky Sport Italia. “We didn’t have time to recover from the first penalty. We tried to push in the end, but the third goal made it even harder for us.” The coach was pushed on his squad rotation, as while the Milan reserves were enough to see off RB Salzburg 4-1 , a Premier League team like Bournemouth are a very different proposition. “There was no game. It’s not about rhythm or Salzburg, there was no game. It is a different team, you cannot have a penalty in that corner and you cannot get sent off in that situation,” he replied with irritation. BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Mike Maignan of AC Milan is shown a red card by Referee Vassilis Fotias after a foul during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) Both the errors were on corners and Maignan with his experience ought to know better than to shove Adams in the face, especially under new rules where the ball doesn’t have to be in play for a penalty to be awarded. “That is true, we cannot do that. We need to keep 11 players on the pitch, there are more experienced players, but now we need to recover and get ready for the next game. We have to run a lot with one less player, try to press at the right moment in that situation, so it was a negative in all aspects tonight.” BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Justin Kluivert of Bournemouth scores his team’s first goal from the penalty spot past Mike Maignan of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Mic
