We have to run a lot with one less player, try to press at the right moment in that situation, so it was a negative in all aspects tonight.” BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Justin Kluivert of Bournemouth scores his team’s first goal from the penalty spot past Mike Maignan of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Usually when a team goes a man down, they try to go 4-4-1, but in this case Amorim tried to keep his three at the back turning into five under pressure. “First of all, they know this way of defending, and as I said they tried to push in the final minutes and not take as many risks during the central part of the game,” replied the coach. “I try to put my players in the most comfortable position and try to change the game with substitutions.” BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, interacts with Mike Maignan after he receives a red card during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Did Amorim speak to Maignan following the dismissal? “No, I didn’t have the time, now I need to go to Milan to prepare for the next match against Udinese. We’ll talk about it when we get back.” Milan had already shown some weaknesses in their 3-2 win over Atalanta at the weekend, as they risked fumbling a 3-0 advantage at San Siro. BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 21: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan addresses the media during the press conference one day ahead of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 at Vitality Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Now they are chasing in the Europa League after losing two of their first three games, also falling 2-0 at home to Benfica in the opening fixture. After 100 days of his Milan tenure, how does Amorim view the situation? “This is part of the journey. If you look at the story of Milan, we are at a different point. Fabio Capello is talking about the history of Milan, and I understand that, but we must be realistic. I appreciated the way we fought, we tried to do something, to help each other out, so we must learn from these moments, realise this is football.”

item.title: Rangers Given Clear Warning Over Celtic Title Race: Can McInnes Exploit Their European Advantage?
item.description: Rangers Given Clear Warning Over Celtic Title Race: Can McInnes Exploit Their European Advantage? Rangers have little room for another domestic slip-up if they want to close the gap on Celtic in the Scottish Premiership. With no European fixtures to manage, Derek McInnes’ side have a clear advantage in their pursuit of the league leaders, but recent results suggest they still need greater consistency. The Ibrox side missed a valuable opportunity last weekend. Rangers surrendered a lead to draw 2-2 against Dundee on October 17, allowing Celtic to strengthen their position with a crushing 7-1 victory over Hearts the following day. That result left the Light Blues four points behind their city rivals, increasing the pressure ahead of Saturday’s home match against St Johnstone. According to comments reported in the Scottish football discussion on The Breakdown podcast, relayed by BBC , former Rangers midfielder Kevin Thomson believes the fixture schedule should favour McInnes’ team over the coming weeks. Rangers have no continental matches after their European qualifying campaign ended in defeat on penalties against Jablonec. Celtic, meanwhile, have at least six more Europa League fixtures to negotiate, beginning with Thursday’s home meeting with Celta Vigo. Thomson argued that playing before Celtic allows Rangers to put their rivals under pressure. A victory against St Johnstone could cut the deficit to one point before Martin O’Neill’s side visit Hibernian on Sunday. The former midfielder also suggested that Rangers could supply more players than Celtic in a combined Old Firm starting XI, reflecting his confidence in the squad’s individual quality. “The bit I think that favours Rangers, or it should, and there can’t be any excuses from a blue perspective, is they’ve not got Europe,” former Rangers midfielder Thomson said on The Breakdown podcast. “The likelihood is they’re going to play in front of Celtic week after week. It’ll not happen every week, obviously. But it’s that psychological aspect of being able to win on the Saturday. “It’s St Johnstone at Ibrox on Saturday and if Celtic were to potentially have a hard European game (against Vigo) and then they have to go to Easter Road on Sunday. They could still go to Easter Road and win, but I think that’s the exciting part about this title race.” Thomson, in a discussion with former Celtic player Charlie Mulgrew about a combined current Old Firm XI, added: “I still think you would pick more Rangers players (than Celtic) in a starting 11 now.” Can Rangers turn their scheduling advantage into a title-winning run? But it’s that psychological aspect of being able to win on the Saturday. “It’s St Johnstone at Ibrox on Saturday and if Celtic were to potentially have a hard European game (against Vigo) and then they have to go to Easter Road on Sunday. They could still go to Easter Road and win, but I think that’s the exciting part about this title race.” Thomson, in a discussion with former Celtic player Charlie Mulgrew about a combined current Old Firm XI, added: “I still think you would pick more Rangers players (than Celtic) in a starting 11 now.” Can Rangers turn their scheduling advantage into a title-winning run? GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – SEPTEMBER 13: Rangers manager Derek McInnes celebrates at full time after a 3-0 victory during the Rangers v Celtic – Premier Sports Cup match at Ibrox Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) McInnes must make that advantage count on the pitch. Rangers have collected 20 points from nine league matches, recording six wins, two draws and one defeat while scoring 13 goals and conceding seven. Five victories in their previous six league games had strengthened their position before the frustrating draw at Dundee interrupted their progress. The defensive record offers encouragement, but Rangers need an efficient attacking threat when opponents defend deep. Their European absence gives the squad more recovery time, yet fatigue alone won’t determine the title race. Celtic can still win domestic matches after demanding European nights, as their demolition of Hearts demonstrated. Rangers, therefore, need to concentrate on their own performances rather than wait for their rivals to stumble. Saturday’s match is important. Dropping points against St Johnstone would waste another opportunity to narrow the gap and hand Celtic greater freedom on Sunday. McInnes must demand a convincing performance, clinical finishing and concentration until the final whistle. Thomson’s argument makes sense, but the psychological advantage works both ways. Winning first can unsettle Celtic; failing to do so can expose Rangers to greater scrutiny. With 20 points already secured, the Ibrox side remain firmly involved in the contest, although their next domestic performance must justify the confidence surrounding their title ambitions.

item.title: Giants’ J.J. McCarthy drops game-changing Jaxson Dart revelation as he replaces Jameis Winston
item.description: Julian Leshay Guadalupe/NorthJersey.com / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Giants’ J.J. McCarthy drops game-changing Jaxson Dart revelation as he replaces Jameis Winston appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Giants recently announced that JJ McCarthy would be replacing Jameis Winston as the team’s starting quarterback for this week’s game against the Houston Texans. The news comes after McCarthy took over for Winston down the stretch of last week’s game vs the New Orleans Saints and nearly led the team on a miraculous comeback. Now, McCarthy has spoken about his relationship with Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart , whose injury opened the door for Winston to become the starter in the first place. “I talked to him today, just normal conversation. We’re both just rooting for each other. And like I told him, I’m doing the same thing that you want, is help win the football games for this organization and do everything we can and be the best versions of ourselves every day to help the collective,” he said, per Giants.com. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCarthy also spoke on how Dart is helping him out with the X’s and O’s ahead of his first start in New York. “It’s going to be great because he is such a smart player and obviously very well-rounded in this offense. It’s going to be awesome to just ask him really anything and pick his brain about anything,” he said. McCarthy was acquired by the Giants from the Minnesota Vikings earlier this season shortly after Dart’s injury, giving New York an insurance policy in case Winston’s struggles continued, which they certainly did. McCarthy overcame an early interception to put up some elite production against the Saints down the stretch on Sunday, nearly pulling off a comeback for the ages in that one. Now, he’ll be matched up against a Texans defense that was arguably the best in the league last year and has now started to round back into form this year. Related: Giants HC John Harbaugh’s J.J. item.title: Hamilton Recalls Meets for African GP as He Makes Call for ‘Congo, Sudan, Syria, Palestine’
item.description: Lewis Hamilton is pleased to see the African GP make a return to the F1 calendar, but he has reservations about Rwanda amid calls for ‘free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine’. Between the races in Singapore and Austin, the FIA, together with FOM, announced the return of the African GP to the F1 calendar from the early 2030s , after signing a long-term deal with the Rwandan government under the Visit Rwanda banner. Even though Rwanda is a regional African nation, it has taken up the ‘African GP’ name, which holds a larger commercial value . Naturally, Ferrari’s Hamilton is pleased to see the return of the Grand Prix that he had been pushing for several years. Hamilton Recalls Countless Meetings to Push Africa Back on F1 Calendar He revealed numerous calls made to Stefano Domenicali and even various heads of African nations. “I’ve been advocating for a race in Africa for many, many, many years,” Hamilton said in the press conference ahead of the F1 US GP. “I have had countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with Stefano at his office in London, but also race weekends. “Countless calls. ‘What’s happening?’, ‘where are we going?’, ‘who are you meeting with?’. Many meetings with different presidents from different countries, lots of phone calls with different presidents in different countries within Africa. For me, it’s a place that deserves to have a Grand Prix. “It’s [about] more than just one country; it is about the continent in itself, and there are so many beautiful countries within it, and the people are so lovely. The culture is so rich, and I think it’s important that we get to show that to the world, and we get to do that with our sport. “We get to go to all these different countries, and people see some of these countries they didn’t really know too much about and all of a sudden it’s on the screen, and kids are talking about it. They go to school talking about it. So, I’m really, really hopeful for that Grand Prix,” summed up Hamilton. Proposed African GP Circuit | Photo Credit: F1, FOM, FIA Amnesty International On Rwanda Situation With Congo But Rwanda potentially hosting an F1 Grand Prix has certainly ruffled a section, especially the Democratic Republic of Congo. Amnesty International believes that Rwanda is undertaking war crimes together with the M23 militia in Congo. They are committing horrific human rights abuses, targeting miners in Congo for gold and cotton. The items are trafficked across the border into Rwanda, with M23 acting as the enforcer at the behest of the Rwandan government. Hamilton is aware of the news and is hopeful that African nations can unite as one in the future. He knows he can’t neglect what is happening not just in Africa but around the globe. In fact, he made the call in the FIA press conference, which often tries to keep it apolitical, even though the call for humanity shouldn’t be mixed with politics. They go to school talking about it. So, I’m really, really hopeful for that Grand Prix,” summed up Hamilton. Proposed African GP Circuit | Photo Credit: F1, FOM, FIA Amnesty International On Rwanda Situation With Congo But Rwanda potentially hosting an F1 Grand Prix has certainly ruffled a section, especially the Democratic Republic of Congo. Amnesty International believes that Rwanda is undertaking war crimes together with the M23 militia in Congo. They are committing horrific human rights abuses, targeting miners in Congo for gold and cotton. The items are trafficked across the border into Rwanda, with M23 acting as the enforcer at the behest of the Rwandan government. Hamilton is aware of the news and is hopeful that African nations can unite as one in the future. He knows he can’t neglect what is happening not just in Africa but around the globe. In fact, he made the call in the FIA press conference, which often tries to keep it apolitical, even though the call for humanity shouldn’t be mixed with politics. Hamilton is Aware as He Makes a Rare Call Using FIA Platform Hamilton also pushes for more knowledge about various historical happenings around the globe that are not taught in schools in England. “Of course, I don’t get to choose where we go, and naturally there are problems all over the world today,” he continued. “I’ve seen many of the stories, but I think we really have to approach it with humility. “There’s a lot that we don’t know. Growing up in England, they never ever taught us anything about Africa. It needs to be on the curriculum: a lot of the problems they have there are still results of colonialism and the West intervening. But if you see people, you see so many designs that are out there today; top brands come from Africa, and it’s got all the richest resources. “I really hope, and I still have hopes, that Africa unites. I know there are many people that don’t want that to happen because they would be so powerful if they did, but I’m still hopeful that at some stage they will. Of course, going doesn’t mean that you neglect the things that are happening there. “So, hopefully many people will start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there, what has happened there for hundreds of years, and I hope that does spark the conversation. I guess I’ll finish it off with: I think we need to make sure we’re pushing to free Congo, free Sudan, free Syria, free Palestine. I think there’s a lot of peace that I’m hoping that at some stage we get to,” summed up Hamilton. Hamilton Hopes to Be Racing Until 2030 to be Able to Race in Africa While he is happy that Africa is finally making a return, he joked about having to stay fit until the 2030s and keep racing to be part of the returning F1 African GP. It is still about four seasons away, and Hamilton is already 41 years old. He will be 45 years old by the time the first race takes place. “I mean, I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer, because we have a race in Africa,” said Hamilton. “And that’s been my dream to be able to race in Africa. I mean, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”

item.title: Kramaric shines as Hoffenheim stun Lyon in the Europa League
item.description: Hoffenheim's Andrej Kramaric celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the UEFA Europa League soccer match between TSG 1899 Hoffenheim and Olympique Lyon at SNP Arena. (is associated with: «Kramaric shines as Hoffenheim stun Lyon in the Europa League») Uwe Anspach/dpa Andrej Kramaric had a brilliant evening as Hoffenheim stunned Ligue 1 leaders Lyon in a 3-0 triumph on Thursday to claim their first win in the Europa League this season. The Germans took the lead shortly before the break as Tim Lemperle's throw-in was loose inside the box until the ball found Kramaric, who headed it into the goal. Adam Daghim then doubled their advantage in the 49th. Kramaric received the ball near the penalty area and passed it to the left, where Noham Kamara accidentally set up Daghim, who cleverly slotted the ball into the lower-left corner. Hoffenheim were finally able to celebrate the three points once Adam Hložek sealed the win in the 83rd. The German side intercepted a sloppy pass from Lyon and the ball again ended up with Kramaric, who served Hložek's effort. The victory comes as huge relief for Hoffenheim. Before Thursday's game, they had only won three out of nine games in all competitions - none of them in the Europa League.

item.title: Emirati diplomat could become next UN chief despite human rights concerns
item.description: Human rights defenders are sounding the alarm over the United Arab Emirates’ nomination of its former envoy Lana Nusseibeh to be the next UN Secretary General. They say electing a diplomat from the UAE, a country with a questionable human rights record that is accused of backing forces behind a massacre in Sudan, could spell “catastrophe” for the UN.

item.title: 🔥Celta pull off a memorable comeback at Celtic Park
item.description: 🔥Celta pull off a memorable comeback at Celtic Park Celta de Vigo secured an epic 2-1 victory over Celtic in Scotland, earning their first three points of the European campaign under Claudio Giráldez. Second-half comeback The hosts took the lead early in the second half through a goal from Baur. However, Celta's response was swift: academy graduate and defender Javi Rodríguez emerged as the night's hero, scoring a decisive brace in just five minutes. Three precious points in Europe Thanks to well-judged substitutions by the coaching staff and key saves from goalkeeper Radu, Celta held on to their lead. After this European triumph, Celta are now turning their attention to Sunday's clash with Betis. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: 49ers’ perfect DeForest Buckner trade offer to Colts before NFL trade deadline
item.description: Image Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images 49ers’ perfect DeForest Buckner trade offer to Colts before NFL trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers should offer the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 third-round pick for DeForest Buckner before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. That is a meaningful price for a 32-year-old defensive tackle, but his production and fit make a reunion worth pursuing. This would not be about correcting an unpopular decision from six years ago. It would be about acquiring an interior difference-maker for a championship push while giving Indianapolis a valuable asset for its next roster overhaul. Why Buckner would elevate San Francisco’s defensive front Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Buckner has recorded 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended through six games in 2026. He also has eight quarterback hits and four tackles for loss. Those numbers show a veteran still influencing possessions rather than surviving on reputation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That interior disruption is what San Francisco should prioritize. Edge pressure becomes more dangerous when quarterbacks cannot comfortably step forward, and Buckner can challenge guards while creating less predictable escape routes. His arrival would also broaden the defensive coordinator’s options. The 49ers could pursue pressure with four rushers more confidently, preserving additional defenders in coverage instead of depending on extra blitzers to manufacture disruption. There is a run-defense benefit, too. Buckner’s ability to penetrate can force runners to alter their paths before reaching the second level. That creates opportunities for teammates, provided the entire front maintains its gap responsibilities. Familiarity adds appeal without eliminating the adjustment period. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco, and Kyle Juszczyk has publicly encouraged him to return. Existing relationships could help his integration, although the current scheme and personnel still require study. The contract creates urgency and risk. Buckner is in the final year of his deal, so San Francisco would be acquiring immediate help without guaranteed control beyond this season. An extension could be discussed separately, but the trade should make sense even without one. It would be about acquiring an interior difference-maker for a championship push while giving Indianapolis a valuable asset for its next roster overhaul. Why Buckner would elevate San Francisco’s defensive front Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Buckner has recorded 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended through six games in 2026. He also has eight quarterback hits and four tackles for loss. Those numbers show a veteran still influencing possessions rather than surviving on reputation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That interior disruption is what San Francisco should prioritize. Edge pressure becomes more dangerous when quarterbacks cannot comfortably step forward, and Buckner can challenge guards while creating less predictable escape routes. His arrival would also broaden the defensive coordinator’s options. The 49ers could pursue pressure with four rushers more confidently, preserving additional defenders in coverage instead of depending on extra blitzers to manufacture disruption. There is a run-defense benefit, too. Buckner’s ability to penetrate can force runners to alter their paths before reaching the second level. That creates opportunities for teammates, provided the entire front maintains its gap responsibilities. Familiarity adds appeal without eliminating the adjustment period. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco, and Kyle Juszczyk has publicly encouraged him to return. Existing relationships could help his integration, although the current scheme and personnel still require study. The contract creates urgency and risk. Buckner is in the final year of his deal, so San Francisco would be acquiring immediate help without guaranteed control beyond this season. An extension could be discussed separately, but the trade should make sense even without one. Why Indianapolis should consider moving its defensive leader The Colts are 2-4, making their deadline decision more complicated than simply declaring themselves contenders or sellers. Trading Buckner would weaken the defense immediately and remove an established locker-room presence. Still, Indianapolis must weigh that loss against the possibility of watching him leave in free agency. A guaranteed third-round selection would provide a concrete return now rather than relying on an uncertain future compensatory-pick outcome. That selection could help address several needs. The Colts could draft a replacement defender, strengthen another position or use it as part of a larger transaction. Younger contributors on rookie contracts would give the organization greater flexibility around its next core. Financial considerations matter, but neither team should confuse Buckner’s full 2026 cap charge with the amount transferred in a deadline trade. Previously paid bonus accounting and remaining compensation require separate analysis before any agreement. The perfect offer balances impact against rental risk The proposed package should remain straightforward: 49ers receive : DT DeForest Buckner Colts receive : San Francisco’s 2027 third-round draft pick. For Indianapolis, a third-rounder acknowledges that Buckner remains a premium contributor rather than a veteran being discarded. For San Francisco, it preserves first- and second-round selections while addressing an immediate need with a proven player. The 49ers should resist adding another substantial asset unless competing bids justify it. Buckner’s age and expiring contract impose a sensible ceiling, even with his strong performance. This is the kind of calculated aggression contenders should embrace: pay for present impact, respect the long-term cost and avoid letting familiarity replace disciplined evaluation. item.title: Half-Life 3 Rumors Reignite After Valve Employee Lets Codename Slip
item.description: It's been two decades since we last checked in on Gordon Freeman in Half-Life 2: Episode Two , with the promise of a third Half-Life game languishing for an absurdly long time. In the intervening years, Valve has neither confirmed nor denied a third mainline Half-Life game, though the secretive studio is rumored to have canceled at least one attempt to make Half-Life 3 . Surprisingly, there's fresh evidence of a new Half-Life game directly from Valve, though the person revealing that information seemingly didn't intend to.

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
item.description: null On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight. "I'm just glad I was able to bring a little happiness to the family," he said, according to Newsweek . The Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-52) launches from NASA's Kennedy Space Center on Oct. 22, 1992. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered The launch of Roddenberry's ashes into space on NASA's STS-52 mission aboard the space shuttle Columbia marked the world's first " space burial ," but it wouldn't be the last. About five years after Roddenberry's memorial flight, in 1997, the space memorial company Celestis began launching a series of "burial" flights by flying capsules with human cremains on rockets . In fact, more of Roddenberry's ashes flew on Celestis' "founders flight" in April 1997 aboard an air-launched Pegasus rocket that took off from the Canary Islands in Spain. The ashes of Roddenberry's wife and of Star Trek actor James Dooha n have also flown in space, among others. Celestis has gone on to launch human cremains on many suborbital and orbital flights, including some on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. The company even launched the ashes of the late astronomer Eugene Shoemaker to the moon in 1999 on the Luna 1 flight, with another set of cremains launched into deep space on the Enterprise mission in 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: 2027 Election: Even Tinubu Knows Atiku Is The Best Candidate – Momodu
item.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communications of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign, Dele Momodu, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as the best candidate for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Momodu said Atiku had been the most deliberate and focused candidate since he first sought the presidency in 1993. The ADC chieftain claimed that President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), also knows that the former vice president is better suited for the job. “When I say he (Atiku) is the best, it is a statement of fact and even President Bola Tinubu himself knows that,” Momodu said. “That is why at a time, he invited him and they joined hands for Atiku to run in the past.” ﻿ Comparing the credentials of the three major presidential candidates, Momodu said Tinubu’s strongest credential was his tenure as governor of Lagos State, while Atiku’s was his experience as vice president and Peter Obi’s as governor of Anambra State. He argued that Tinubu had underestimated the differences between governing Lagos and leading Nigeria. “So, if you look at the three mainstream candidates today, the APC candidate Bola Tinubu, the ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar and the NDC candidate Peter Obi, you can judge for yourself. Bola Tinubu came, his best credential was being the former governor of Lagos State; Atiku came, his best credential was being the former vice president of Nigeria; Peter Obi came, his best credential was being the governor of Anambra State. “So, if you judge for yourself, you will know that perhaps what has happened to President Tinubu is the fact that when he got to the Presidency, he assumed that Nigeria was Lagos and he soon discovered that Nigeria is different from Lagos and that is why he’s had total commotional confusion and his guys are running all over the places throwing money around.” Momodu also accused the Tinubu administration of failing to be sincere with Nigerians, alleging that officials around the President were more concerned with telling him what he wanted to hear than confronting him with the realities facing the country. “What is lacking in this government is that sincerity. Everything is about one man. The people who are running our economy today have to tell Nigerians only what they think the president wants to hear. They are not telling him the truth, and when tomorrow comes, he will realise it,” he added. The post 2027 Election: Even Tinubu Knows Atiku Is The Best Candidate – Momodu appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. You can only beat what lies in front of you and Marco Rose’s players never relinquished control against a rotten impersonation of a Milan side. The visitors resembled holograms even before Mike Maignan, their goalkeeper, rendered their task impossible with a deserved sending-off in the first half. By then Justin Kluivert had given Bournemouth the lead with a penalty and it was another spot-kick from Marcus Tavernier, given after Maignan’s rush of blood, that underlined their overwhelming superiority. Amine Adli applied the garnish with a late free-kick and it meant an abject return to British shores for Ruben Amorim, who would have been excused seeing this particular week as the opportunity to make a point. On this evidence Manchester United, to whom Bournemouth travel on Sunday, share more than a few similarities with the modern version of Milan. Continue reading...

item.title: FG to bar defaulting contractors from public procurement for five years
item.description: The Federal Government has directed the strict implementation of the National Guideline on Debarment of Contractors, Consultants and Service Providers. The directive is contained in a circular issued by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Sen. George Akume, with reference number 59780/S.2/B/585. This is according to a statement by Ngozi Anyaelezu, Acting Head of Public Relations, Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), in Abuja on Thursday. Anyaelezu said that the guidelines provide for the exclusion of defaulting contractors from public procurement for up to five years. She said the circular mandated all Accounting Officers in Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to ensure full compliance with the guidelines. “It aims to prevent fraud and corruption in contract execution by ensuring that contractors who violate the provisions of the Public Procurement Act, 2007, are promptly reported and excluded from further participation in government procurement.” The guidelines said that the BPP may initiate debarment proceedings following findings from its reviews, surveillance or audits, or based on a properly supported recommendation from a procuring entity approved by its Accounting Officer. It provides that an affected contractor must be notified of the allegations and given 10 working days to respond, with provision for a limited extension in appropriate circumstances. “Where the Debarment Committee establishes a case against a contractor, it may impose a debarment period of between three years and five years. “A debarred contractor will be prohibited from being invited to bid for or awarded Federal Government contracts. “The contractor will also be barred from conducting government business as an agent or representative of another contractor, consultant or service provider.” The guideline further provides that the name of every debarred entity will be entered into the BPP database and published on the Bureau’s website, the Federal Tenders Journal and other relevant platforms. It, however, allows for the reinstatement of debarred contractors after the expiration of the sanction, subject to an application supported by evidence of reform. “The Federal Government reiterated its commitment to transparency, accountability and fiscal discipline in public expenditure. “All Accounting Officers are to ensure that the guidelines are brought to the attention of Tenders Boards, Procurement Planning Committees, procurement departments and all officers involved in public procurement.” Meanwhile, following the circular, Dr Adebowale Adedokun, Director-General of the BPP, said the guideline was designed to eliminate corrupt, fraudulent and non-performing contractors from the public procurement system. Adedokun said the measure would safeguard public funds and promote value for money in government expenditure. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: The Federal Government has directed the strict implementation of the National Guideline on Debarment of Contractors, Consultants and Service Providers. The directive is contained in a circular issued by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Sen. George Akume, with reference number 59780/S.2/B/585. This is according to a statement by Ngozi Anyaelezu, Acting Head of Public Relations, Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), in Abuja on Thursday. Anyaelezu said that the guidelines provide for the exclusion of defaulting contractors from public procurement for up to five years. She said the circular mandated all Accounting Officers in Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to ensure full compliance with the guidelines. “It aims to prevent fraud and corruption in contract execution by ensuring that contractors who violate the provisions of the Public Procurement Act, 2007, are promptly reported and excluded from further participation in government procurement.” The guidelines said that the BPP may initiate debarment proceedings following findings from its reviews, surveillance or audits, or based on a properly supported recommendation from a procuring entity approved by its Accounting Officer. It provides that an affected contractor must be notified of the allegations and given 10 working days to respond, with provision for a limited extension in appropriate circumstances. “Where the Debarment Committee establishes a case against a contractor, it may impose a debarment period of between three years and five years. “A debarred contractor will be prohibited from being invited to bid for or awarded Federal Government contracts. “The contractor will also be barred from conducting government business as an agent or representative of another contractor, consultant or service provider.” The guideline further provides that the name of every debarred entity will be entered into the BPP database and published on the Bureau’s website, the Federal Tenders Journal and other relevant platforms. It, however, allows for the reinstatement of debarred contractors after the expiration of the sanction, subject to an application supported by evidence of reform. “The Federal Government reiterated its commitment to transparency, accountability and fiscal discipline in public expenditure. “All Accounting Officers are to ensure that the guidelines are brought to the attention of Tenders Boards, Procurement Planning Committees, procurement departments and all officers involved in public procurement.” Meanwhile, following the circular, Dr Adebowale Adedokun, Director-General of the BPP, said the guideline was designed to eliminate corrupt, fraudulent and non-performing contractors from the public procurement system. Adedokun said the measure would safeguard public funds and promote value for money in government expenditure. He said that the government would no longer tolerate compromises that undermined the integrity of public procurement processes. The director-general said that any Accounting Officer or procuring entity that bypassed the debarment registry or violated the provisions of the Public Procurement Act would face administrative and legal sanctions. “Moving forward, all procuring entities are mandated to verify compliance,” he said. He said the guidelines identify several grounds for debarment, including offering money, gifts or other benefits to influence procurement decisions, and providing employment or financial benefits to procurement officials for improper purposes. “Other grounds include conviction for fraud relating to public contracts, falsification of documents, and wilful or persistent failure to fulfil contractual obligations. “It also allows the Federal Government to consider for debarment contractors already sanctioned by multilateral organisations,” he said. (NAN) The post FG to bar defaulting contractors from public procurement for five years appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obasanjo’s son joins Tinubu Must Stay Movement
item.description: Olujonwo Obasanjo, son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, has joined the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, pledging to promote policy continuity and explain President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. He announced his decision at a news conference in Abuja on Thursday, where the leadership of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS) welcomed him. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that TMS is a political advocacy platform promoting policy continuity, sustainable governance and public understanding of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Olujonwo said his decision was shaped by his political experience, understanding of Nigeria’s reform history and belief in sustaining government policies across administrations. “I’ve been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu to form the movement. I’m not new to the party,” he said. He said inadequate communication about the Tinubu administration’s policies had created opportunities for misinformation and misinterpretation among Nigerians. “There’s a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what’s going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students now have access to education loans. “Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote,” he said. Olujonwo said communicating government policies required explaining their objectives, implementation processes and implications for citizens rather than relying solely on political slogans. The National Coordinator of TMS and Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Abdullahi, welcomed him into the movement. Abdullahi said Olujonwo’s family background gave him an understanding of economic reforms and their implications for national development. “You grew up in a family that led the second wave of reforms in Nigeria. Telecommunications liberalisation and banking reforms — these laid a solid foundation. “Being raised in that family, you understand what reforms mean,” he added. Abdullahi said policy consistency was essential for national development, warning that frequent reversals could undermine investor confidence and disrupt long-term planning. “We are building investors’ confidence; the naira is becoming strong, our stock exchange is one of the fastest-growing. “The Dangote Refinery is a game changer. If we start reversing these policies, we’ll go back to where we were,” Abdullahi said. He said TMS would expand its nationwide structures and engage stakeholders across professional, political and social groups. Abdullahi said the movement supported policy continuity beyond 2027, while seeking to strengthen institutional development and the sustainability of government programmes. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: Olujonwo Obasanjo, son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, has joined the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, pledging to promote policy continuity and explain President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. He announced his decision at a news conference in Abuja on Thursday, where the leadership of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS) welcomed him. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that TMS is a political advocacy platform promoting policy continuity, sustainable governance and public understanding of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Olujonwo said his decision was shaped by his political experience, understanding of Nigeria’s reform history and belief in sustaining government policies across administrations. “I’ve been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu to form the movement. I’m not new to the party,” he said. He said inadequate communication about the Tinubu administration’s policies had created opportunities for misinformation and misinterpretation among Nigerians. “There’s a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what’s going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students now have access to education loans. “Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote,” he said. Olujonwo said communicating government policies required explaining their objectives, implementation processes and implications for citizens rather than relying solely on political slogans. The National Coordinator of TMS and Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Kashifu Abdullahi, welcomed him into the movement. Abdullahi said Olujonwo’s family background gave him an understanding of economic reforms and their implications for national development. “You grew up in a family that led the second wave of reforms in Nigeria. Telecommunications liberalisation and banking reforms — these laid a solid foundation. “Being raised in that family, you understand what reforms mean,” he added. Abdullahi said policy consistency was essential for national development, warning that frequent reversals could undermine investor confidence and disrupt long-term planning. “We are building investors’ confidence; the naira is becoming strong, our stock exchange is one of the fastest-growing. “The Dangote Refinery is a game changer. If we start reversing these policies, we’ll go back to where we were,” Abdullahi said. He said TMS would expand its nationwide structures and engage stakeholders across professional, political and social groups. Abdullahi said the movement supported policy continuity beyond 2027, while seeking to strengthen institutional development and the sustainability of government programmes. The Director-General of TMS, Marcel Ngogbehei, described Olujonwo’s entry as significant, citing his family’s association with economic reforms and democratic consolidation. Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient movement, recalled former President Obasanjo’s telecommunications liberalisation policies and Nigeria’s external debt relief. He said those reforms helped lay the foundations for subsequent economic development. “We are happy you have decided to take this step. Your father was one of those who revolutionised this country. “The debt was paid off, and major innovations were introduced in liberalising the economy,” he said. Ngogbehei said TMS was established to encourage informed public engagement on government policies, address misconceptions about ongoing reforms and promote assessments based on evidence and measurable outcomes. item.title: UEL: Juventus denied at the death, Sunderland make point in Poland
item.description: Bayer Leverkusen made it three straight wins in the Europa League with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games. Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. The Blacks Cats took a second-half lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win. With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ men. In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor’s 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. The Blacks Cats took a second-half lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win. With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ men. In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor’s 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts. item.title: Tinubu appoints Yusuf Bichi chairman of NISS governing board
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appointed Y. M. Bichi, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Abuja. Bichi’s appointment, based on the recommendation of the current DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, takes effect from October 22, 2026, for an initial four-year term. According to a statement by the Director of Coordination and Liaison, NISS, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, the appointment was made in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019. Bichi succeeds A. A. Gadzama on the governing board. He handed over leadership of the DSS to the incumbent director-general in August 2024. Before his appointment as DSS director-general, Bichi began his career in the Security Division of the Kano State Cabinet Office before his transfer of service in 1984. His appointment brings experience in intelligence, security administration, operational leadership and institutional training to the governance of the institute. The post Tinubu appoints Yusuf Bichi chairman of NISS governing board appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: After Starshield interruption, Ukraine wants to build its own satellite communication network with ICEYE and Nokia
item.description: null Ukraine wants its own satellite-communication system, which shouldn't be surprising given the events of the past week or so. The Ukrainian military just signed a letter of intent with two Finnish companies — the telecom giant Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE — to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communications network for Ukraine. "Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls," ICEYE cofounder and CEO Rafal Modrzewski said in a statement today (Oct. 22). "We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. ICEYE has proudly supported Ukraine since 2022, and we remain committed to continuing that support today." Ukraine relies heavily on satellite-based communications and data to defend itself from Russia, which invaded the nation in February 2022 and continues to attack it with ground troops, missiles and drone strikes. But Ukraine does not own those satellites. It primarily uses the services provided by SpaceX's Starlink megaconstellation in low Earth orbit (LEO) and Starshield , a military-grade, jamming-resistant version of Starlink employed by the U.S. government and its allies. Starshield in particular is crucial to Ukraine, as it allows the nation to operate fast-moving drones over large distances in war zones. Ukraine has gotten very good at drone warfare, employing these little robots both in offensive and defensive capacities. On Oct. 14, however, Ukrainian soldiers and officials reported a severe throttling of their access to Starshield services — a speed limit on terminal-carrying drones, which caused many of them to fall out of the sky . It's not entirely clear who's behind the throttling. Some U.S. officials have apparently said the order came from Elon Musk , but the billionaire SpaceX founder and CEO put the ultimate responsibility on the Trump administration. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk said on Oct. 14 via X, the social media platform he owns. Whoever made the call, it certainly wasn't Ukraine. And the Starshield throttling — which apparently is still in effect — has doubtless reinforced the nation's desire to control its own satellite-communications infrastructure. "Nations need communications they can rely on in every situation. Satellite networks extend and protect connectivity when networks on the ground are disrupted," Mikko Hautala, Nokia's chief geopolitical and government relations officer and chairman of Nokia Defense, said in the same statement. "This makes them a key part of any secure communications system," he added. "Through this Letter of Intent, together with Ukraine and ICEYE, we will explore how trusted, sovereign satellite communications can strengthen Ukraine's resilience and give it control over the connectivity it depends on." item.content:encoded: null Ukraine wants its own satellite-communication system, which shouldn't be surprising given the events of the past week or so. The Ukrainian military just signed a letter of intent with two Finnish companies — the telecom giant Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE — to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communications network for Ukraine. "Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls," ICEYE cofounder and CEO Rafal Modrzewski said in a statement today (Oct. 22). "We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. ICEYE has proudly supported Ukraine since 2022, and we remain committed to continuing that support today." Ukraine relies heavily on satellite-based communications and data to defend itself from Russia, which invaded the nation in February 2022 and continues to attack it with ground troops, missiles and drone strikes. But Ukraine does not own those satellites. It primarily uses the services provided by SpaceX's Starlink megaconstellation in low Earth orbit (LEO) and Starshield , a military-grade, jamming-resistant version of Starlink employed by the U.S. government and its allies. Starshield in particular is crucial to Ukraine, as it allows the nation to operate fast-moving drones over large distances in war zones. Ukraine has gotten very good at drone warfare, employing these little robots both in offensive and defensive capacities. On Oct. 14, however, Ukrainian soldiers and officials reported a severe throttling of their access to Starshield services — a speed limit on terminal-carrying drones, which caused many of them to fall out of the sky . It's not entirely clear who's behind the throttling. Some U.S. officials have apparently said the order came from Elon Musk , but the billionaire SpaceX founder and CEO put the ultimate responsibility on the Trump administration. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk said on Oct. 14 via X, the social media platform he owns. Whoever made the call, it certainly wasn't Ukraine. And the Starshield throttling — which apparently is still in effect — has doubtless reinforced the nation's desire to control its own satellite-communications infrastructure. "Nations need communications they can rely on in every situation. Satellite networks extend and protect connectivity when networks on the ground are disrupted," Mikko Hautala, Nokia's chief geopolitical and government relations officer and chairman of Nokia Defense, said in the same statement. "This makes them a key part of any secure communications system," he added. "Through this Letter of Intent, together with Ukraine and ICEYE, we will explore how trusted, sovereign satellite communications can strengthen Ukraine's resilience and give it control over the connectivity it depends on." Nokia and ICEYE announced on Oct. 1 that they plan to work together to help nations develop such sovereign satcom systems. The partnership with Ukraine follows on from that earlier agreement. Russia's Luch-2 satellite approaches another geostationary satellite on April 12, 2024, as tracked by the French company Aldoria's observation stations. (Image credit: Aldoria) ICEYE has already been aiding the Ukrainian defense effort. The Finnish company and its U.S. subsidiary jointly operate a fleet of Earth-observing satellites in LEO, which study our planet using synthetic aperture radar. Ukraine uses data from the ICEYE constellation for intelligence and planning purposes. This relationship has put ICEYE — or one of its satellites, at least — in Russia's crosshairs. A Russian inspector satellite called Kosmos 2612 recently made an extremely close approach to ICEYE-X36 , which is operated by ICEYE US. The goal of the unsanctioned rendezvous is unclear. Russia may have wanted to assess the satellite's capabilities or interfere with it in some way. Or perhaps the nation simply wanted to send a message, letting ICEYE (and Ukraine) know that it could mess with satellites if it wanted to.

item.title: The FCC is beginning to block gadgets with ‘foreign surveillance chips’
item.description: On October 13th, Brendan Carr's FCC gave itself a new power - it can block gadgets for containing any computer chip made by any company on its list of potential threats to national security . Today, it's exercising that power for the first time, blocking two gadgets because they contain "foreign surveillance chips," the FCC claims . item.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
item.description: eMudra, the certificate authority that issued eight intermediate TLS credentials so weak that anyone could mint certificates for any website or mail server—one had a private encryption key of just 4—said it’s getting out of the business. V. Srinivasan, chairman of India-based eMudhra Limited, cited increasing costs and complexities of compliance requirements—paired with the business generating just 1 percent of its revenue. He also said that the emergence of organizations providing TLS certificates free of charge further reduced returns on investment when compared to other products and services the company offers. Don't let the door hit you on the butt “However, the level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” the company continued in a Thursday post. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Everything We Know About Project Helix, the Next Xbox
item.description: The results have been chaotic: a leadership change, mass layoffs, the closure and divestment of several studios. Console exclusivity for first-party was seemingly abandoned, but is now (partially) back on the menu. Game Pass is in flux, with multiple changes in bundling and pricing strategy, and more on the way. Microsoft has finally solved the drought of first-party games that plagued it during the Xbox One era and the first years of the Xbox Series — but, ironically, it seems to have nowhere useful to put all those games.

item.title: The 2027 total solar eclipse will plunge these 10 ancient Egyptian temples and monuments into darkness
item.description: null The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. Modern Luxor, population 285,000, is set to become a focal point for eclipse chasers on Aug. 2, 2027, and will attract many thousands of international visitors. They'll come for the forecasted 0% chance of clouds and the era-defining duration of totality, but also to tour ancient Egypt's temples and monuments. The chances of actually witnessing totality at any of the major temples are probably slim. Still, almost every eclipse chaser headed to Luxor will want to tour them before or after the eclipse. Visitors should be prepared for extreme August heat and check official opening and access arrangements before planning to watch the eclipse at any archaeological site. Certified eclipse glasses are essential during the partial phases; only during totality, when the sun is completely covered, is it safe to look without them. Ancient monuments in the path of totality Not all of ancient Egypt will experience totality. Egypt's top-ranking monument, the Pyramids at Giza, near Cairo, lies north of the path of totality and will get a 95% partial solar eclipse. Abu Simbel, on the shores of Lake Nasser south of Aswan, will also see a 92% partial solar eclipse. No matter, Luxor is home to some of the world's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments. Here are its temples, necropolises and palaces — and those nearby, also in the 160-mile (257-kilometer)-wide path of totality — that will have the moon's umbral shadow fall upon them on Aug. 2, 2027. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Karnak Temple Karnak Temple in Luxor will be the hottest ticket in the world on Aug. 2, 2027. (Image credit: Frank Fell/robertharding via Getty Images) Location: East bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:02 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% Dedicated to the god Amun-Ra — a fusion of the hidden god of the sun Amun and the ancient sun god Ra — this vast temple complex will be the hottest ticket in town for the eclipse. One of Egypt's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments, it's a place designed by ancient astronomers — the winter solstice sunrise still illuminates the innermost sanctuary. Access arrangements for eclipse day have yet to be confirmed, so keep an eye on official announcements before making plans

Ancient monuments in the path of totality Not all of ancient Egypt will experience totality. Egypt's top-ranking monument, the Pyramids at Giza, near Cairo, lies north of the path of totality and will get a 95% partial solar eclipse. Abu Simbel, on the shores of Lake Nasser south of Aswan, will also see a 92% partial solar eclipse. No matter, Luxor is home to some of the world's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments. Here are its temples, necropolises and palaces — and those nearby, also in the 160-mile (257-kilometer)-wide path of totality — that will have the moon's umbral shadow fall upon them on Aug. 2, 2027. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date . 1. Karnak Temple Karnak Temple in Luxor will be the hottest ticket in the world on Aug. 2, 2027. (Image credit: Frank Fell/robertharding via Getty Images) Location: East bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:02 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% Dedicated to the god Amun-Ra — a fusion of the hidden god of the sun Amun and the ancient sun god Ra — this vast temple complex will be the hottest ticket in town for the eclipse. One of Egypt's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments, it's a place designed by ancient astronomers — the winter solstice sunrise still illuminates the innermost sanctuary. Access arrangements for eclipse day have yet to be confirmed, so keep an eye on official announcements before making plans to watch totality from the complex. 2. Luxor Temple Luxor Temple's obelisk will point almost straight at the eclipsed sun. (Image credit: Roberto Moiola / Sysaworld via Getty Images) Location: East bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:02 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% This is one of Egypt's best-preserved ancient temples and a must-see during the 2027 eclipse. It's on the banks of the Nile near the city center, so it's relatively easy to visit. Dedicated to the god Amun, it is known for its beautiful pillars and intricate carvings. A 75-foot (23 meters) tall obelisk on the east side of its entrance will point at the eclipsed sun almost directly overhead on Aug. 2, 2027. Its missing right-hand obelisk is in the Place de la Concorde, Paris. 3. Valley of the Kings KV9, the tomb of Ramesses V & Ramesses VI, in the Valley of the Kings, Luxor. (Image credit: Brandon Rosenblum via Getty Images) Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% This incredible necropolis is home to the tombs of the pharaohs and is a testament to the advanced engineering and architectural skills of the ancient Egyptians. Of course, you don't want to be underground for totality, but some of the tombs are a must-see. Your tickets include entry to any three tombs of your choice from those open that day, with extra tickets available for the really impressive ones—the spectacular KV17 (Seti I), small but iconic KV62 (Tutankhamun), and KV9 (Ramesses V & VI). The latter's Corridor G has a ceiling decoration that may depict a deep partial solar eclipse from 1143 BC. 4. Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut The Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut offers space, but little shade. (Image credit: Paul Biris via Getty Images) Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% If one temple is best suited to crowds for an eclipse, it's this vast, open-air gem dedicated to the legendary queen who became pharaoh. However, with almost no shade, it could be the least practical option. Three huge terraces rise above the desert floor and into the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari to the west. It's an absolute masterpiece. 5. Colossi of Memnon The Colossi of Memnon are often relatively quiet. (Image credit: Tuul & Bruno Morandi via Getty Images) Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% This is where we get to temples that are fairly well known, but likely won't have as much pressure on them from eclipse chasers as the big three — Karnak, Luxor and Hatshepsut. However, anyone looking for ways to get temple architecture into images of an eclipse at zenith should look no further than these two large stone statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III. Behind them are the ruins of the largest temple in the Theban Necropolis. 6. Medinet Habu Aerial view of the Medinet Habu in Luxor, Egypt. (Image credit: nomadnes via Getty Images) Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Chance of clouds: 0% Getting off the beaten track in August 2027 will be near-impossible, but here's an option — the Mortuary Temple of Ramesses III. Featuring towering stone columns, colorful reliefs (despite being 3,200 years old) and famous carvings, it's bypassed by tour buses heading straight for Hatshepsut. 7. Ramesseum The funerary temple of Rameses II, the Ramesseum. (Image credit: Gian Berto Vanni via Getty Images) Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% Another temple that, without Karnak and Luxor nearby, would be rammed with visitors, is the Ramesseum — the mortuary temple of Ramesses II. Featuring the remains of a huge fallen statue that inspired Shelley's poem Ozymandias , it's in an area once used by the artisans who built the royal tombs, and slightly off the tourist route. 8. Temple of Khnum The colorful ceilings at the Temple of Khnum in Esna. (Image credit: Brandon Rosenblum via Getty Images) Location: Esna, Egypt Start of totality and duration : 1:02 p.m. EEST; 5 minutes, 47 seconds Historical cloud cover: 0% If you want to avoid the scrum of eclipse chasers in Luxor on and around Aug. 2, the Temple of Khnum could be an option. Located in Esna, about 34 miles (55 kilometers) south of Luxor, the so-called 'Rainbow Temple' (for its colorful ceilings) is dedicated to the ram-headed creator god Khnum. Dating from the Greco-Roman era, there's a vast Hypostyle Hall that sits below modern street level, which could be good for some shade. 9. Temple of Dendera The Temple of Dendera is among Egypt's best-preserved and most beautiful. (Image credit: nomadnes via Getty Images) Location: Qena, Egypt Start of totalit

item.title: Tinubu Tasks Medical Experts On Brain Drain Solutions In West Africa
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to develop practical and sustainable solutions to medical brain drain across the sub-region, warning that the migration of skilled professionals continues to put pressure on healthcare systems. He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. According to a statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu spoke on Thursday after being conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja. He urged the College’s leadership to use its forthcoming conference to develop lasting solutions to the challenge. “We are more challenged in Africa than anywhere else; you know, and with the outbreak of Ebola now we’re looking for a preventive action that will eliminate all these problems and infections. So, I wish you the best. As I pledge to behave myself, I will continue to do whatever I can do for this honourable profession,” the President said. Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to comprehensive health sector reforms aimed at making healthcare delivery more accessible, affordable and efficient for Nigerians. He also commended the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, for driving the reforms. “We as a government are doing everything possible. Please help me congratulate the reform-oriented physician, Ali Pate, who has been doing a very good job,” he said. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency The President acknowledged medical professionals’ contributions to medical research, disease prevention, life-saving interventions and the development of resilient healthcare systems capable of responding to existing and emerging health challenges. He thanked the College’s leadership for considering him worthy of the honour. The WACP conferred the fellowship on Tinubu in recognition of his contributions and commitment to strengthening healthcare reforms and medical development in Nigeria. The College President and Chairman of its Board of Trustees, Dr Mamadou Mourtala Ka, said the fellowship was reserved for presidents who had made significant contributions to healthcare delivery across the sub-region. “This award is given only to presidents who have made a mark in health care delivery and affected the health of the West African people,” he said. The College’s Secretary-General and spokesperson for the delegation, Professor Musa Dankyau, said the decision reflected the administration’s commitment to far-reaching health sector reforms. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026. item.content:encoded: President Bola Tinubu has urged the West African College of Physicians (WACP) to develop practical and sustainable solutions to medical brain drain across the sub-region, warning that the migration of skilled professionals continues to put pressure on healthcare systems. He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. According to a statement by presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu spoke on Thursday after being conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja. He urged the College’s leadership to use its forthcoming conference to develop lasting solutions to the challenge. “We are more challenged in Africa than anywhere else; you know, and with the outbreak of Ebola now we’re looking for a preventive action that will eliminate all these problems and infections. So, I wish you the best. As I pledge to behave myself, I will continue to do whatever I can do for this honourable profession,” the President said. Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to comprehensive health sector reforms aimed at making healthcare delivery more accessible, affordable and efficient for Nigerians. He also commended the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, for driving the reforms. “We as a government are doing everything possible. Please help me congratulate the reform-oriented physician, Ali Pate, who has been doing a very good job,” he said. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency The President acknowledged medical professionals’ contributions to medical research, disease prevention, life-saving interventions and the development of resilient healthcare systems capable of responding to existing and emerging health challenges. He thanked the College’s leadership for considering him worthy of the honour. The WACP conferred the fellowship on Tinubu in recognition of his contributions and commitment to strengthening healthcare reforms and medical development in Nigeria. The College President and Chairman of its Board of Trustees, Dr Mamadou Mourtala Ka, said the fellowship was reserved for presidents who had made significant contributions to healthcare delivery across the sub-region. “This award is given only to presidents who have made a mark in health care delivery and affected the health of the West African people,” he said. The College’s Secretary-General and spokesperson for the delegation, Professor Musa Dankyau, said the decision reflected the administration’s commitment to far-reaching health sector reforms. President Tinubu was conferred with a Fellowship of the WACP at the State House, Abuja on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency Dankyau said the College had awarded the fellowship only eight times in its 50-year history. He named former Gambian President Dawda Jawara as the first recipient and said former Nigerian Head of State, General Ibrahim Babangida, received the honour in 1991. “So, this is the second time we are coming back to Nigeria to present to you, Mr President. The Council has noted your significant contributions to health infrastructure, improved access to care and emergency care, and massive investments in primary health care and universal health coverage. “At the last count, over $2.2 billion had been invested in that area for the health of the Nigerian people. We’ve also seen significant strides in disease prevention, immunisation and public health preparedness. Just a couple of days back, the health minister had also announced that we are ready and prepared to face Ebola. And so, we were able to reassure our colleagues,” Dankyau said. The meeting was attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume; Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila; Professor Pate; Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris; and Special Adviser to the President on Health Matters, Dr Salma Ibrahim Anas. The WACP also informed Tinubu of its 50th anniversary celebration and Annual General Scientific Meeting, scheduled for October 26 to 28, 2026, at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja. item.title: Sid Meier's Civilization games: the oral history
item.description: Sid Meier (Creator of Civilization, co-founder of MicroProse and Firaxis): I was always playing with toys as a child. I remember spreading my blocks and soldiers and ships over the living room floor until my mom said, “Somebody’s coming over — you gotta clean up!” And I had an interest in history; I read about airplanes and ships, pirates, for example. As I got a little older, I got into board games and strategy games. This was all before computers appeared. When computers appeared, my first computer was the Atari 800. Whoa, I can make my own game s. That was super cool.

item.title: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing
item.description: Those mourning yesterday's shuttering of highly praised and influential developer BioWare also had to deal with the cancellation of the next Mass Effect game, which was first teased back in 2020 . Today, we got our best look at what that game could have been with a short, leaked trailer for Mass Effect: Universe . In the roughly two-minute montage—which describes itself as "in-engine footage from our small team" that "uses our pre-production assets"—an ex-military officer wearing an N7 trenchcoat (similar to the one seen in that 2020 teaser) encounters an Asari at a bar. He talks of his frustration with military life—"by the time you put out one fire, another had already started"—before discussing his new line of work "stopping [the fires] before they start" and "making the choices no one else is willing to make. Going where others are afraid to go." Mass Effect: Universe Trailer by u/Random_Hyabusa_Ninja in masseffect Read full article Comments

item.title: ‘The best on Earth’: Can weak economic growth undermine Europe’s ‘very sophisticated social system’?
item.description: Can Europe continue to sustain one of the world's most ambitious social models while falling increasingly behind its major economic competitors? For Pascal Lamy, former European Commissioner for Trade and former Director-General of the World Trade Organization, this question lies at the heart of the continent's mounting economic and political tensions. Lamy looks beyond the immediate turmoil in France to identify a deeper European predicament: a widening disconnect between the continent's social commitments and its capacity to generate the economic growth needed to sustain them.
