item.title: 2027: Leave Pope, church out of political campaigns, Obi tells opponents
item.description: By Henry Umoru Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC ahead of the 2027 elections, Peter Obi has urged political opponents to keep the Pope, Pope Leo XIV and the Catholic Church out of partisan campaigns. The former Anambra State governor condemned in very strong terms the circulation of an artificial intelligence-generated image allegedly showing him and an Enugu State governorship candidate seeking Pope Leo XIV’s blessing for electoral victory, describing the image as misleading and unwarranted. In a statement signed on Thursday by the Spokesman of his Campaign Media Office, POMR, Idris Zekeri, Obi said the office had become aware of the image depicting Cardinal John Onaiyekan and described in the statement as the NDC presidential candidate, and Sir Chinyeaka Oha, the party’s Enugu State governorship candidate, standing before the Catholic Pontiff. The statement condemned the alleged use of artificial intelligence to create the image and urged political actors to refrain from involving religious leaders and institutions in partisan disputes. Obi maintained that his political campaign focused on addressing Nigeria’s pressing challenges, including poverty, insecurity, corruption and economic hardship. He also highlighted the need to expand opportunities for young people and build a country where citizens could live with dignity and hope. He challenged political opponents to focus their campaigns on policy issues, records and leadership capacity rather than religious controversies. He expressed disappointment over the incident, insisting that the 2027 general election should centre on Nigeria’s future and the issues affecting citizens, just as he also called for the Pope and the Catholic Church to be allowed to carry out their spiritual responsibilities without being drawn into partisan political disputes. The statement read, “The Peter Obi Media Office has become aware of a deceptive AI-generated image depicting the NDC Presidential Candidate, revered Cardinal John Onaiyekan, and the Enugu State NDC gubernatorial candidate, Sir Chinyeaka Oha, standing before the Catholic Pontiff, Pope Leo XIV, and seeking his blessing for electoral victory. “The Media Office strongly condemns this conduct and calls on political opponents to stop involving the Holy Father, the Pope, and the Catholic Church in partisan campaigns. Such an act is misleading and entirely unwarranted. “The Church is a sacred institution that must be respected rather than exploited for political gain. Peter Obi’s campaign is centred on issues. It seeks to rescue Nigeria from poverty, insecurity, corruption, and economic hardship; expand opportunities for our youths; and build a nation in which every Nigerian can live with dignity and hope. “He also welcomes vigorous political debate and challenges his opponents to address Nigerians on these urgent matters. “Let us debate our records, policies, competence, character, and vision for the country.” “The 2027 election

item.title: 2027: APC will campaign on achievements, not insults – Gov. Yusuf
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf has promised that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will focus on issues, achievements and plans rather than personal attacks in its campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Yusuf gave the assurance on Thursday during the inauguration of the APC 2027 presidential and gubernatorial campaign council management team in Kano. He said the party would explain its achievements to voters, present its plans for the future and listen to the needs of the people. “We are going to campaign based on what the APC leaders have done, not campaign full of insults,” the governor said. Yusuf said members of the campaign council were selected based on their capacity to carry out the responsibilities assigned to them. He urged them to work hard to ensure that the APC secured more votes in Kano than in any other state during the 2027 elections. “Kano should garner a lot of votes for President Tinubu. The number of votes the APC gets in Kano should be the highest in the country. This is possible if you go out and campaign as required,” he said. The governor described the council members as representatives of the party who must work towards securing victory for the APC and President Bola Tinubu. “The members of this council are APC soldiers, and I urge you to carry out your responsibilities with commitment and work towards the party’s victory,” Yusuf said. He also urged them not to be intimidated by opposition parties or allow fear to affect their campaign activities, insisting that the APC had established itself in the state. Yusuf appealed to party members and supporters whose names were not included in the initial campaign council list not to feel disappointed, explaining that additional lists and subcommittees would be announced. He called on party members to remain committed and work together to mobilise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. Among the key appointments, Abdullahi Tijjani Muhammad Gwarzo was named Director-General of the campaign council, while Hon. Bala Muhammad Gwagwarwa will serve as First Deputy Director-General. Dr. Yunusa Adamu Dangwani was appointed Deputy Director-General for Kano South, while Dr. Ali Haruna Abubakar Makoda and Senator Abdussalam Abdulkarim Zaura will serve as Deputy Directors-General for Kano North and Kano Central, respectively. Dr. Mariya Mahmoud Bunkure was also named Assistant Director-General for Women Affairs, while Hon. Garba Yusuf Abubakar will serve as Assistant Director-General for Operations, among other appointments. Stakeholders present at the event included Senators Kawu Sumaila and Barau Jibrin, as well as Mariya Bunkure. The post 2027: APC will campaign on achievements, not insults – Gov. Yusuf appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Curfew imposed in certain areas of Paris every night until Monday morning
item.description: The curfew has been extended in certain areas of Paris, every night from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. until Monday morning. The measure has been in force since the violence and looting of the weekend, according to an order from the Paris police prefecture published Thursday. A Paris protest Thursday organised by students -- who had held four weeks of protests before the October 17 rallies -- went ahead with hundreds attending after a police ban was overturned by an emergency court injunction. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Alice Cohen-Morzadec, International Spokesperson of "L'Union étudiante."

item.title: APC using statistics to tell lies, fighting on all fronts — Dele Momodu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communications of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign, Dele Momodu, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of using economic statistics to mislead Nigerians, alleging that President Bola Tinubu’s administration is fighting criticism from international institutions while struggling to win public confidence ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Momodu, who is backing ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, made the remarks on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, while questioning the government’s presentation of economic figures and the credibility of the electoral process. “I saw the speech of an Emir in the North, I wish we had a lot of time, I would have read it to you. They were told the brutal truth that you should never lie to the people. What the APC is doing today is to use those statistics to tell lies and to say The World Bank are for us, The IMF are for us,” he said. So they are fighting on all fronts,” Momodu said. Yesterday, I saw your guest, a senator of APC, boasting, we have 12 million registered members of our party. And the next party has maybe about 4 million registered voters. “But INEC is telling us we have 103 million registered voters. So tell me, will 12 million people override the will and wishes of 103 million people?” he asked. Momodu argued that Nigerians who were not firmly aligned with any political party could play a decisive role in the election, describing them as the “floaters party”. “What that tells you immediately is that the largest political party in Nigeria, it’s not APC, it’s not ADC, it is the floaters party and the floaters are the ones crying today that their lives are in a big mess,” he said. ‘Hunger’ can defeat Tinubu Momodu also blamed a lack of sincerity within the government for what he described as shortcomings in economic management, arguing that officials were not giving the president the full picture. “What is lacking in this government is that sincerity. Everything is about one man. The people who are running our economy today have to tell Nigerians only what they think the president wants to hear. item.title: Israel’s Ben-Gvir shares AI videos mocking Gazans as ‘donkeys’ and sending them to Paris
item.description: Israel’s far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir is using AI-generated videos to mock Palestinians and push political messages ahead of the country’s election, including videos magically transporting Gazans to Paris or calling them "donkeys" for choosing to stay. One video has sparked an online spat with France. AI is playing a growing role in the campaign, with parties using deepfakes, bots and AI-generated content, raising concerns about disinformation and the technology’s influence on voters.

item.title: Stop announcing how much your movie made at the cinema — Filmmaker Biodun Stephen tells colleagues
item.description: Nollywood filmmaker Biodun Stephen has urged colleagues to stop announcing cinema earnings, warning that the practice puts unnecessary pressure on other filmmakers and creates a narrow definition of success in the industry. Stephen made the remarks during Paul & Baaj: In Character podcast, where she argued that publicising box office figures could distract filmmakers from focusing on the quality and impact of their work. “I think that we really should do away with the announcements,” she said. “I feel like this is a distractions and it puts pressure on those other people who… feel as if that is the determine and that’s how you determine my success,” she added. The filmmaker explained that frequent announcements of cinema earnings could make others feel unsuccessful if their projects failed to achieve similar figures. Using a slippers business as an example, Stephen said people often rush to replicate successful ventures without understanding the effort and strategy behind them. “Somebody starts selling slippers and people are rushing to buy slippers, the next one… is going to sell slippers… because they think that slippers sells, meanwhile they don’t understand what you have put in to ensure the slipper sells.” Biodun Stephen also questioned the tendency among some filmmakers and actors to pursue international recognition before establishing a strong presence in Nigeria. “It’s great to hunger for more, but I always say, have you even conquered Nigeria that can you stand and say that if I go to Kano they know me as an actor?” She further argued that box office earnings alone were insufficient to determine a film’s quality, longevity or potential to reach international audiences. According to her, a film could generate substantial cinema revenue without necessarily being outstanding, while a well-made production with export potential might earn less and receive little recognition. “The film go tough but it can be a lot of crap and then the film that is really good that can travel, that has export value can do 40 million… the only yard stick for measuring success is this very shallow number.” Explaining her approach to filmmaking, Stephen said her motivation was rooted in purpose rather than the pursuit of box office records or audience numbers. “I’m doing it because I am living a life of purpose, I’m not chasing the numbers, I’m not chasing the audience.” She added that the emotional impact of her stories and the difference they made in people’s lives were more meaningful to her than industry awards. “When people call me to pray… and cry and say thank you so much, Jesus, my work is done, no award.” Vanguard News The post Stop announcing how much your movie made at the cinema — Filmmaker Biodun Stephen tells colleagues appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
item.description: A 25-year-old German experimental photographer has won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with a striking image of droplets of ink being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. Ole Bielfeldt beat out 1,802 other entries hailing from 69 different countries. Bielfeldt became interested in photomicrography during the COVID-19 lockdown after discovering an old microscope in his parents' attic. He figured out how to build an adaptor out of a tube and some wood to connect the microscope to his father's camera and taught himself the art through trial and error, building custom tools as needed. He documents how he captures transformative images of everyday objects with behind-the-scenes videos posted to macrofying , his photography and videography brand. It was Bielfeldt's curiosity about the inner workings of inkjet printers that inspired his winning entry, but capturing the action of ink drops being deposited on paper was a challenge, given that the process happens so quickly. The droplets, for instance, moved faster than the camera's shutter speed. Bielfeldt's solution was to deconstruct the printer so that the paper moved under a stationary (rather than moving) printhead, and then take the image in a dark room, using a flash to serve as the shutter, thereby freezing the ink drops mid-air. There was no need for pricey equipment. Bielfeldt does not use AI in his images, preferring to rely on traditional techniques. Read full article Comments

item.title: Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' after Ramaswamy attack ad in Ohio governor's race
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday defended an explosive attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign against his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race, telling fellow Republicans to "stop whining" about it and go win the race. The ad features ​Democrat Amy Acton’s ‌estranged mother, Donna Arthur, disputing Acton’s account of a childhood she says involved a period of homelessness and sexual abuse. ⁠Arthur, whom Acton says she has not seen since 1978, urges Ohioans not to vote for her daughter. Acton has said she was sexually abused by her stepfather when she was 12. Her mother stayed with the ‌stepfather, who was charged with rape but fled the state and was never tried. He died in 2004. Acton said she ⁠and her brother were removed from her mother's custody for severe abuse, neglect and sexual abuse. Acton's brother has supported her account. FRANCE 24's Catherine Viette reports.

item.title: "Disillusioned" MAHA leader quits as Trump admin's food agenda spoils: Report
item.description: Calley Means—a top ally to anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a co-author of the so-called "MAHA bible"—resigned from his role in the Trump administration Thursday, reportedly in frustration over delays to food policy changes sought by the Make America Healthy Again movement. "I am resigning from the White House with tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy," Means wrote in a social media post this afternoon . "It was an honor to advocate for MAHA moms in the administration and steer policies like Dietary Guidelines reform, psychedelic reform, removing soda from SNAP, removing food dyes, GRAS reform, and overhauling government food procurement." His post did not provide a reason for his departure. Means served as a senior advisor to Kennedy. Read full article Comments

item.title: Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State capital, Makurdi, has been thrown into darkness following the withdrawal of services by members of the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, in the Jos Electricity Distribution Plc, JED, chapter, over an alleged attack on some of its members by suspected armed men. The union alleged that the attackers invaded the Makurdi District office of JED, seized the Benue State Operating Officer, Mr. Samson Abah, and an unspecified number of other workers before taking them to the River Benue Bridge, where they were reportedly assaulted. According to the union, the attackers also seized the workers’ mobile phones and other personal belongings, demanded money for their release and allegedly forced them to reconnect electricity supply to the Benue State Government House. The Acting National Secretary of NUEE, Dominic Igwebike, who disclosed this in a statement, said the incident followed the disconnection of electricity supply to Government House over an alleged discovery of meter bypass by government officials. The union’s position came amid an escalating disagreement over electricity supply to the state government’s seat of power, with the Benue State Government dismissing the allegations and accusing JED of making unsubstantiated claims against it. Igwebike said the union could no longer guarantee the safety of its members if they continued to work under the prevailing circumstances, insisting that the withdrawal of services was necessary to protect their lives and property. He said, “Our members cannot continue to work under their brutalised, intimidation and threats to life until we are assured of the safety of our lives and properties.” Confirming the shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, a JED staff member, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak on the matter, said the workers withdrew their services following the alleged attack on their colleagues. “Our office was attacked and our union asked us to withdraw our services, so we have shut down power supply to Makurdi. We have left the office after shutting down, and Makurdi will not have power supply until the matter is resolved with our union,” the staff member said. However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image. In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Chief Solomon Iorpev, the government said it would not accept allegations linking it to violence, abduction or illegal electricity connections without credible evidence. The statement read, “The Government of Benue State strongly rejects the baseless and defamatory allegations contained in the press statement issued by Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED Plc) on October 22, 2026. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.” Addressing

However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image. In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Chief Solomon Iorpev, the government said it would not accept allegations linking it to violence, abduction or illegal electricity connections without credible evidence. The statement read, “The Government of Benue State strongly rejects the baseless and defamatory allegations contained in the press statement issued by Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED Plc) on October 22, 2026. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.” Addressing the allegations surrounding the reported attack on JED workers, the government questioned the evidence linking it to the incident, arguing that the distribution company had not provided verifiable details to substantiate its claims. According to the statement: “JED Plc’s own use of the word ‘allegedly’ confirms that it has no evidence linking the Government to the incident of October 21, 2026. No names, identities, or credible references were provided. The Government categorically rejects this insinuation.” On the dispute over electricity supply to Government House, the state government said issues concerning transformer energisation and alleged metering irregularities should be handled through the appropriate regulatory and judicial channels. It stated, “Issues of transformer energization and metering irregularities are regulatory matters. They must be addressed before the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts, not through inflammatory press releases. “Assertions of abduction, assault, and injuries remain unsubstantiated. The Government does not condone violence and demands that impartial, evidence-based, and transparent investigations be carried out by security operatives,” the statement added. Expressing displeasure over JED’s handling of the controversy, the government described the company’s public reaction as premature, arguing that it should have allowed security agencies to establish the facts before making allegations in the media. “The reckless outburst by the JED without conclusive investigations is suspicious and amounts to sponsorship by enemies of state to tarnish the image of the government,” the statement alleged. The government also faulted JED’s reference to an earlier incident on September 3, 2026, describing the company’s account as misleading. It challenged the distribution company to produce documentary evidence of its alleged previous communications with the state government over the dispute. “The company has failed to produce records of its alleged ‘several communications’ with the Government. The State challenges JED Plc to publish such correspondence if it exists,” the statement said. Insisting that electricity distribution companies must comply with the same regulatory requirements and safety standards applicable to their customers, the government said JED must also be held accountable for its operations. The statement added: “JED Plc itself acknowledges that interventions must comply with regulatory requirements and safety standards. The Government insists that this standard binds JED Plc as firmly as it binds any customer, including public institutions.” The state government further warned JED against what it described as attempts to politicise its operations and damage the integrity of the state. “The Benue State Government will not tolerate attempts by any business entity to politicize its operations or malign the integrity of the State. JED Plc is hereby strongly warned to desist from making baseless accusations in the media,” it said. Consequently, the government demanded the immediate withdrawal of what it described as the insinuation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of the allegation that it engaged in meter bypassing or illegal electricity connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State. It warned that it would consider legal action if JED persisted in disseminating what it described as false information. “The Government remains committed to the rule of law, the protection of lives and property, and constructive engagement with stakeholders in the electricity sector. However, it will not hesitate to pursue legal remedies should JED Plc persist in disseminating falsehoods,” the statement said. The government added that the people of Benue State deserved reliable electricity supply, respectful treatment and accountability rather than what it termed reckless allegations. As of the time of filing this report, the dispute had resulted in a shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, with the workers insisting that they would not resume operations until the matter was resolved with their union. item.title: S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse
item.description: By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police. While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday. The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly. Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations. He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training. Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property. The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters. Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people. According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.” Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state. Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities. item.content:encoded: By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police. While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday. The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly. Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations. He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training. Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property. The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters. Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people. According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.” Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state. Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities. He said the establishment of state police would help “curtail incessant violence and herdsmen attacks in different parts of the state.” However, the member representing Igbo-Eze South Constituency, Hon. Harrison Ogara, cautioned that the proposed state police system could be abused by political officeholders if adequate safeguards were not established. Ogara expressed concern that state police formations might be used to intimidate political opponents, stressing that effective oversight and accountability mechanisms were necessary to protect the institution from political interference. He said: “State Police formations could be used to intimidate political opponents if adequate safeguards are not put in place.” The lawmaker also called for professional standards, transparent accountability structures and sustainable funding arrangements to ensure that state police personnel discharge their duties without undue political influence. According to him, effective oversight would be essential to ensuring that the proposed security structure serves the public interest rather than the interests of those in power. The Speaker of the House, Chief Uche Ugwu, said the proposed changes to the naming of Nigeria’s policing institutions could also influence institutional orientation and the attitudes of personnel. The proposal includes changing the name of the Nigeria Police Force to the Federal Police Service, alongside the establishment of the State Police Service. Ugwu said the changes could contribute to a shift in institutional orientation and personnel attitudes, potentially improving the delivery of policing services. The proposed constitutional amendment comes amid growing calls for the decentralisation of Nigeria’s security architecture to enable states to respond more effectively to local security challenges. Proponents argue that state police would improve intelligence gathering and response times, while critics have raised concerns about possible political abuse, inadequate funding and the need for strong accountability mechanisms. Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill. Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny. He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large. The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing. “We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said. Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard on Thursday afternoon that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill. He disclosed that the Bill had already received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it will ultimately be passed into law. He said that the passage of the Bill into law would help address peculiar security challenges of every state as every state better understands its own terrain more than strangers. Later in the day, the Abia State House of Assembly voted in favour of the State Police Bill. The Acting Clerk Abia State House of Assembly, Mr Promise confirmed this in an interview with Vanguard. Speaking later with Vanguard, Deputy Speaker Nmeregini, said that the State Police Bill was passed by “unanimous vote.” The post S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
item.description: BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the new X5 and iX5, as well as a refreshed i7 (which you can read about soon). Ars does not accept paid editorial content. When we first drove BMW’s first Neue Klasse model, the iX3 , it quickly revealed that BMW knows how to make a good electric vehicle. A clean-sheet design, it featured the automaker’s sixth-generation electric powertrain , a completely reimagined dashboard, and powerful computers to run the whole show. Now, much of that technology is being ported over to the larger X5 line. But BMW knows not all its customers are ready to go electric, especially in the US, so it’s sticking with its powertrain-agnostic CLAR platform, as used in cars as diverse as the large 7 Series and the new gasoline 3 Series. Which means in addition to the all-electric iX5, there are also mild hybrid and plug-in hybrid X5s available, and in time, even a hydrogen-powered option. For now, as I’ll explain, I think the EV is the pick of the bunch. Get used to it, because this is what BMW SUV kidney grilles look like from now on. Credit: BMW If you looked very carefully you'd see this was an iX5 because there's no exhausts. Of course, reading the badge is probably easier. Credit: BMW Pick your power The most conventional option is the X5 40 xDrive, powered by a 3.0 L turbocharged inline six-cylinder engine that generates 394 hp (294 kW) and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm). The 48 V mild hybrid system can contribute a decent slug of torque (148 lb-ft/200 Nm) if necessary, and the engine operates under the Miller cycle for better efficiency, as well as featuring the usual BMW engine technology, like variable valve timing. Expect around 26 mpg (9 L/100 km) from this powertrain and a full-to-empty range of 569 miles (915 km). Read full article Comments

item.title: Jenna Ortega's New Sci-Fi Movie Turns Compelling AI Drama Into One Big Joke
item.description: Maybe it’s a sign of a more jaded world or a less capable film , but with Klara and the Sun , I found myself wishing for restraint. Don’t make the obvious joke; don’t encourage another weird face-off between actors. A dramatic scene depicting a robot’s devotion to humanity would land better if we could sit with it without a giggle break. But no such luck.

item.title: Discord now formats Markdown previews right
item.description: Discord's latest update released today has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with "a bunch of symbols," according to the company. LLMs and AI agents often rely on Markdown files for instructions and context, so these improved previews could be helpful for people sharing information about AI projects on the platform. "When you upload a Markdown (.md) file, you'll now see the file rendered all nice and neat and pretty instead of with a bunch of symbols," Discord says . "This includes tables, formatting, all that good stuff. Totally great for when you're doing a casual Sunday-night sharing READ … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA
item.description: — Petrol supply drops 20.6% By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries fell by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August, while petrol supply from domestic refineries also declined amid reduced imports. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday showed that average daily petrol receipts dropped by 23.4 per cent to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the decline to lower domestic supply and reduced imports following the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. Between January and September 2026, Nigerian refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic crude accounted for 80.4 per cent of total refinery intake during the period, while imported crude contributed 19.6 per cent. The report also showed that Dangote Refinery operated at 105.98 per cent utilisation in September, processing approximately 689,000 barrels of crude oil per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from the refinery’s inventory, indicating that it processed more crude than it received during the month. On petrol supply, the NMDPRA data showed that domestic refineries supplied an average of 28.5 million litres per day in September, down 20.6 per cent from 35.9 million litres in August. Petrol imports also declined by 30.1 per cent to 10.2 million litres per day from 14.6 million litres. Despite the decline, domestic refineries remained the largest source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts in September, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September average of 38.7 million litres per day was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres of petrol per day, representing 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA reiterated that September’s decline in petrol receipts reflected a 21 per cent drop in domestic supply from August levels and a 30 per cent reduction in imports amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. The post Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
item.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was on Thursday awarded the European Union's top rights prize, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump. "The European Union is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and this prize recognises the important work of the court in upholding international law and justice," said European Parliament chief Roberta Metsola in announcing the award. The ICC thanked the European Parliament for giving it the Sakharov Prize "at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges". FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Edo govt demolishes building allegedly used for organ harvesting, cultism
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu A house in Uwalor-Oke in Uromi, Esan North East Local Government Area of Edo State has been demolished for allegedly being used for cult activities and organ harvesting. Besides the demolition, the suspected organ harvester Ebhata Eromosele was also arrested by the Edo State Special Security Squad codenamed Operation Flush out Kidnapping and Cultists, in collaboration with Edo State Security Corps, the Nigerian Police Force and other sister security agencies, supervised by the Principal Security Officer (PSO) to the governor. The building was said to have been used for ritual activities where Eromosele was alleged to have harvested the organs of three young women, out of which one of the victims, a pregnant woman, died in the process; one who was hospitalised has been discharged while another is receiving treatment in an undisclosed hospital in Esan Central Senatorial District. Another building located at Idi-Negbon Eguare Ewatto, allegedly used for cult-related activities, was also not spared as it was touched by bulldozers. In a statement by Governor Monday Okpebholo’s Chief Press Secretary, Dr. Patrick Ebiojele, the coordinator of the Special Security Squad, Amiolemen Idemudia said criminals would be wiped out of Edo State. He noted that Ebhata Eromosele engaged in ritual activities before nemesis caught up with him and have been arrested and today his building is demolished in Uromi. He said, “A lifeless body killed and dumped was traced by Edo State Security Corps to this bungalow apartment used by the suspect. “A search of this residence exposed the suspect as security operative saw bloodstained bedspread and other incriminating evidence indicating that Ebhata is into ritual activities and organ harvesting.” Idemudia said the governor has warned that his administration will not tolerate crime of this nature and will make the state unsafe for criminal elements. On the cult issue, Idemudia said there were cult fracas in Ewatto disturbing the peace of the community. He said that one Bright Ejetuwamen was at the forefront of the fight, using his properties at Ewatto for cult-related activities. He said the property has been demolished. “Governor Monday Okpebholo will not spare any hideout or properties used to perpetrate crime as it will be demolished. The cultist has been apprehended. All criminals must leave Edo State,” he said. The Zonal Commander, Edo State Security Corps, SP Johnson Oyameda (rtd), said the success recorded in the arrest of the ritual suspect was as a result of over a month of surveillance. “The body of a lady mutilated and dumped in a drainage was recovered while still alive. Not up to two weeks another body was recovered again and these incidents led to stepping up surveillance around the area and the surveillance paid off. “Ebhata Eromosele murdered a lady and dumped the body but my men on surveillance saw him and trailed him to this apartment which has been demolished today,” he said. item.title: Lego Confirms Incredible Daft Punk Set for Official Release
item.description: Lego is officially teaming up with Daft Punk for new "products, content and brand experiences," the toymaker announced Thursday. While Daft Punk (the musical act) split up in 2021, Daft Punk (the brand and trademark) lives on. As part of a new partnership between The Lego Group and the French electronic music duo, a Daft Punk Lego set originally designed by a fan will be released as an official product. But that's apparently just the start of what the brands have in store.

item.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
item.description: Android-powered foldable phones have been available for years, but most people never paid attention to them. As predicted, that could be changing now that Apple has entered the folding phone market with the iPhone Duo . Analysts have speculated that Samsung's Z8 foldables were seeing a boost from the iPhone announcement, and now Samsung has seemingly confirmed that. In a new blog post , Samsung UK crows that the company's 2026 foldable lineup is moving much faster than last year's models. Compared to the Galaxy Z Fold 7, combined European sales for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra are up 45 percent. Samsung isn't talking about Z Flip 8 sales, but it previously noted that its larger foldables made up about 80 percent of foldable purchases. We can assume any increase there is not impressive enough to mention. The reason for flat Z Flip sales may simply be that Apple didn't release a flip phone. Unsurprisingly, Samsung doesn't mention Apple or the iPhone Duo in its press release. However, it does say that search volume for the Z8 series across Europe spiked 460 percent the week of September 6 to 12. And guess what was announced on September 9? Yep, the iPhone Duo. Z Fold 8 search volume across the entire month of September (when the phones launched) was up 260 percent. Read full article Comments

item.title: DSS secures 7th death sentence as Adamawa court convicts three over kidnap of Catholic priests
item.description: A high Court of Adamawa State, on Thursday, sentenced to death three persons who kidnapped two Catholic priests in February 2025. Delivering judgement, Justice Christopher Mapeo found the three men guilty of criminal conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, conspiracy to commit armed robbery, armed robbery, harboring a kidnapped person and negotiating to receive ransom for the release of Reverend Fathers Matthew Dutsemi and Abraham Sauman. The judge sentenced the three men, Taledo Demiel, Namomai Medan and Mikaila Yusuf, to death for kidnapping, armed robbery and other offences.Thursday’s death sentence is the seventh secured by the DSS this year. On 20th May, 2026, Ekiti High Court sentenced two men, Ibrahim Abubakar and Abdullahi Abubakar to death by hanging for kidnapping. About two weeks later, on 3rd June, 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja sentenced to death by hanging, four men who, in June 2022, massacred scores of worshippers at the St. Francis Catholic church, Owo, Ondo State. The convicts are Idris Abdulmalik Omeiza, Alqasim Idris, Jamiu Abdulmalik and Abdulkareem Idris. Less than two weeks later, on 15th June, 2026, a Katsina High Court sentenced a female arms courier, Hauwa’u Mukhtar, to death by hanging. The following day, on 16th June, 2026, a Kogi High Court sentenced Jibrin Halilu to death by hanging for kidnapping and murdering his neighbour in Obajana, an industrial town in the state. About a week after the Kogi sentencing, on 22nd June, 2026, a Sokoto High court sentenced three persons Muhammed Yusuf Sallau, Jabbi Ahlaji Yale and Kabiru Muhammed, to death by hanging, for terrorism and for transporting arms. Less than three months later, on28th September 2026, a Sokoto High Court sentenced Ibrahim Usman aka Dan Iyali to death by hanging over his involvement in the killing of three kidnapped persons in the state. The post DSS secures 7th death sentence as Adamawa court convicts three over kidnap of Catholic priests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Next in line? Main contenders for the Manchester United hot seat
item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation. According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum. The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials. Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister. Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president. However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters. In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum. Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension. The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel. In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity. “Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility. He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules. The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport. The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced. The post Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US official: Russia's stalker satellite sure looks like an orbital weapon
item.description: Four years ago, a senior official in Russia's foreign ministry painted a bullseye on commercial satellite networks that assist Ukraine in its fight against invading Russian military forces. On Wednesday, several days after a Russian military spacecraft moved within striking distance of one of those commercial satellites, the same Russian diplomat assured the world there's no reason to worry. There's a sharp incongruity in those statements from Konstantin Vorontsov, deputy head of Russia's delegation to the United Nations. Vorontsov's comments Wednesday in the UN General Assembly's First Committee came moments after a US official called attention to recent maneuvers by Kosmos 2612 , a Russian military craft that approached a US-registered commercial satellite some 340 miles (550 kilometers) above Earth. Read full article Comments

item.title: DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa
item.description: — Sule commends security agencies over crackdown on arms trafficking By Edwin Philip LAFIA — Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for its sustained efforts to clamp down on gun runners and arms traffickers in the state following the arrest of a 23-year-old female suspected arms courier in Keffi. The governor’s commendation was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by his Press Secretary, Ibrahim Addra, who described the arrest of Aisha Mohammed, a resident of Bwari, Federal Capital Territory, as a significant breakthrough. According to the statement, Mohammed was arrested with 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition and three empty magazines. “The suspect, currently in custody, was arrested while in possession of 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition with three empty magazines,” the statement said. It added that other suspected arms couriers arrested between August and September 2026 included Hassan Sani, 40; Abdulkadir Idrissa, 41; and Salihu Garba, 70, also known as Nabayi. The statement said security operatives recovered 678 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 99 rounds of 7.5mm ammunition and other items from the suspects. It further disclosed that an alleged arms courier, Ismail Lawalli, a native of Zamfara State, was arrested in August along the Keffi-Abuja highway with 1,262 assorted rounds of ammunition. Sule praised DSS personnel and other security agencies in Nasarawa for their dedication and commitment to tackling arms trafficking and other criminal activities. He also commended the collaboration between the security agencies and his administration, pledging continued government support for their operations. The governor assured residents of his administration’s resolve to combat criminality and called on the public to support security agencies in maintaining peace and safety across the state. The post DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager
item.description: By Chioma obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Thursday uncovered another illegal herbal products factory in Agege, Lagos, where three unregistered products were allegedly manufactured under unhygienic conditions, with one bearing a registration number belonging to a registered cough syrup. The agency sealed the facility, evacuated the products and arrested the manager, identified as Abulaziz Sayidu, for interrogation, while the alleged owner, Ashietu Adams, was said to have fled. The Deputy Director in charge of the Pharmaceutical Division, Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, NAFDAC, Pharm. Edith Joseph, who spoke during an inspection of the facility said the agency received intelligence on October 16 concerning the alleged production of Aishetu Adams Bitters with a fake NAFDAC registration number, prompting surveillance and intelligence gathering that led to the discovery of the facility concealed inside a residential building. “What we found was shocking. The facility was in a very poor and unhygienic condition. Look at the water they use for production and the environment where the manufacturing takes place. The products are manufactured outdoors, in the open air. I can tell you that this facility is not approved by NAFDAC,” she said. The products recovered were identified as Ashietu Adams Herbal Mixture for sexually transmitted diseases, Ashietu Adams Blood Purifier and another herbal preparation purportedly used for high blood pressure. Joseph said none of the three products was registered with NAFDAC, adding that the registration number displayed on the blood purifier belonged to a registered cough syrup. “The number belongs to another registered product, which is a cough syrup. They simply copied the number and placed it on their product to deceive Nigerians,” she said. According to her, the products were manufactured without regulatory approval, while their packaging lacked the manufacturer’s name and a verifiable address to establish their origin. She said the agency had sealed the facility pending further investigation and taken the recovered products to its office. Joseph disclosed that Sayidu claimed to have worked with Adams for about a year and assisted in managing the business, particularly when she travelled. The manager reportedly told officials that Adams, whom he identified as a Ghanaian woman, had travelled to Ghana. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Chioma obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Thursday uncovered another illegal herbal products factory in Agege, Lagos, where three unregistered products were allegedly manufactured under unhygienic conditions, with one bearing a registration number belonging to a registered cough syrup. The agency sealed the facility, evacuated the products and arrested the manager, identified as Abulaziz Sayidu, for interrogation, while the alleged owner, Ashietu Adams, was said to have fled. The Deputy Director in charge of the Pharmaceutical Division, Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, NAFDAC, Pharm. Edith Joseph, who spoke during an inspection of the facility said the agency received intelligence on October 16 concerning the alleged production of Aishetu Adams Bitters with a fake NAFDAC registration number, prompting surveillance and intelligence gathering that led to the discovery of the facility concealed inside a residential building. “What we found was shocking. The facility was in a very poor and unhygienic condition. Look at the water they use for production and the environment where the manufacturing takes place. The products are manufactured outdoors, in the open air. I can tell you that this facility is not approved by NAFDAC,” she said. The products recovered were identified as Ashietu Adams Herbal Mixture for sexually transmitted diseases, Ashietu Adams Blood Purifier and another herbal preparation purportedly used for high blood pressure. Joseph said none of the three products was registered with NAFDAC, adding that the registration number displayed on the blood purifier belonged to a registered cough syrup. “The number belongs to another registered product, which is a cough syrup. They simply copied the number and placed it on their product to deceive Nigerians,” she said. According to her, the products were manufactured without regulatory approval, while their packaging lacked the manufacturer’s name and a verifiable address to establish their origin. She said the agency had sealed the facility pending further investigation and taken the recovered products to its office. Joseph disclosed that Sayidu claimed to have worked with Adams for about a year and assisted in managing the business, particularly when she travelled. The manager reportedly told officials that Adams, whom he identified as a Ghanaian woman, had travelled to Ghana. The agency said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the operation and the whereabouts of the alleged owner. NAFDAC WARNS CONSUMERS Joseph warned Nigerians against relying solely on NAFDAC registration numbers when purchasing herbal medicines and other regulated products, noting that counterfeiters could copy legitimate numbers to give unregistered products the appearance of regulatory approval. She advised consumers to verify product details through NAFDAC’s online verification platforms and the agency’s Greenbook. “If the name displayed does not match the product being presented, consumers should know that something is wrong,” she said. She urged consumers, particularly those in rural communities with limited internet access, to visit the nearest NAFDAC office for assistance in verifying the authenticity of products before purchase or consumption. The deputy director identified the absence of a valid registration number, manufacturer’s name and verifiable address as major warning signs, adding that the agency was intensifying surveillance and enforcement operations against illegal manufacturing outlets. Also speaking during the inspection, Deputy Director of Public Relations, NAFDAC, Mrs Christiana Obiazikwor, called for increased public participation in the fight against counterfeit and unregistered products. Obiazikwor warned landlords and property owners against allowing their premises to be used for illegal manufacturing activities, noting that those found to be aiding criminal operations could face prosecution. She urged property owners to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious operations to the appropriate authorities. “We cannot fight this battle alone. Every Nigerian has a role to play in identifying and reporting places where illegal manufacturing activities are taking place,” she said. Obiazikwor said NAFDAC was expanding public awareness through radio programmes, multilingual jingles and community sensitisation campaigns, including its “NAFDAC and Your Health” programme. She said the agency also conducted awareness campaigns in local government areas, churches and schools to educate Nigerians on how to identify suspicious products and report illegal manufacturing activities. Emphasising the importance of product traceability, she said consumers should check details such as the manufacturer’s address and batch number rather than relying solely on a registration number. “These products do not have batch numbers or the manufacturer’s address. These are important details that help establish the identity and traceability of a product,” she said. She added that the agency was working towards stiffer penalties for offences involving the manufacture and distribution of counterfeit and unregistered products. NAFDAC urged members of the public to report suspected illegal manufacturing activities, assuring them that reports would be handled discreetly. item.title: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find
item.description: null Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it. But while this sky happens to perfectly match the one depicted in the artwork, art historians have long thought that Van Gogh painted this piece in June. Could these findings shift the date of this legendary artwork? Finding a painted sky This investigation started decades ago with art historian Albert Boime and astronomer George Abell at UCLA in 1984 and continued in the following years with astronomer Charles Whitney at Harvard University. However, these earlier analyses did not agree with one another, and there was no true consensus about exactly when the sky matched with the painting. So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more. "When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com . A figure from Kim et al.'s paper in Scientific Reports. According to the figure: "The central cluster of stars in The Starry Night (1889), left, and the Hyades cluster in Taurus, center. At right, the five stars in the painting (orange) are overlaid on the real stars (blue) after matching for size, orientation and position; red dashed lines show the residual differences." (Image credit: Kim et al., Scientific Reports (2026)) But how did Kim's team come to their conclusion, after others had failed to nail down a date over the decades? item.dc:creator: Chelsea Gohd
item.content:encoded: null Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it. But while this sky happens to perfectly match the one depicted in the artwork, art historians have long thought that Van Gogh painted this piece in June. Could these findings shift the date of this legendary artwork? Finding a painted sky This investigation started decades ago with art historian Albert Boime and astronomer George Abell at UCLA in 1984 and continued in the following years with astronomer Charles Whitney at Harvard University. However, these earlier analyses did not agree with one another, and there was no true consensus about exactly when the sky matched with the painting. So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more. "When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com . A figure from Kim et al.'s paper in Scientific Reports. According to the figure: "The central cluster of stars in The Starry Night (1889), left, and the Hyades cluster in Taurus, center. At right, the five stars in the painting (orange) are overlaid on the real stars (blue) after matching for size, orientation and position; red dashed lines show the residual differences." (Image credit: Kim et al., Scientific Reports (2026)) But how did Kim's team come to their conclusion, after others had failed to nail down a date over the decades? In short, "we analyzed the painting astronomically, analyzed documents about his situation in July 1889, and then carried out ecological and meteorological investigations," Kim said. To start with, the team analyzed the sky from the exact location in Saint-Rémy where Van Gogh is said to have painted "The Starry Night." They then used observational geometry to map the historical night sky. "Modern telescopes are equipped with a function called astrometry, which compares an image of the night sky with celestial coordinates stored in a computer and automatically extracts the coordinates of the image," Kim said. "We used Procrustes analysis, a method that compares only the 'shape' of two sets of points. After matching their position, size and rotation, it measures how similar the two shapes are from the differences that remain (the residuals)." "Because a star cluster on the canvas may be larger or smaller than in reality and slightly tilted, this method was the right fit. It allowed us to explain, in quantitative terms, what earlier studies had described only qualitatively as 'resembling a certain constellation,'" Kim added. But this quantitative analysis wasn't enough to say for sure that this was the right-fitting sky, as different constellations could fit to a similar degree, Kim explained. To get closer to their answer, the team combined their analysis with a deep dive through history. "We also checked whether the stars were actually in that part of the pre-dawn sky on that date, whether they fall within the painter’s field of view, and whether the appearance of the moon and Venus matches the painting. It was the Hyades that satisfied all of these conditions," Kim said. Exploring astro-art history As mentioned, the date of this matching sky comes in late July, a month after art historians think Van Gogh painted "The Starry Night." But the researchers suggest that their findings could provide evidence to support the idea that the work was actually painted in July. Letters written by Van Gogh as early as 1888 describe his desire to paint a star-filled sky. A letter dated April 12, 1888 reads: "A starry sky, for example, well — it’s a thing that I’d like to try to do, just as in the daytime I’ll try to paint a green meadow studded with dandelions." Kim followed these letters through the months to try and find more information that could potentially alleviate the discrepancy between the matching skies and the actual month the painting was created. Kim pointed to a letter from between late May and early June 1889 that reads: "This morning I saw the countryside from my window a long time before sunrise with nothing but the morning star, which looked very big." Kim drew on "personal imagination" to find ties between Van Gogh's sky observations in these months and what they might mean for the painting's timeline, Kim shared, so this doesn't definitively change the view of this painting's history. However, Kim suggested that these records could indicate that Van Gogh was repeatedly looking up and watching the pre-dawn sky, which could have led to him seeing this exact sky on July 22. The painting itself even ignites uncertainty among art historians. As the researchers cite in their new paper, leading art historians see "The Starry Night" as stylistically different from Van Gogh's other works during the month of June, drawing further questions over the date painted. "What our study shows is that the sky in the painting matches, in both observation and shape, the real pre-dawn sky around July 22. So, what we propose is the possibility that Vincent conceived the idea in June and completed the painting after July 22," Kim said. However, "I think further research in art history and conservation science could shed more light on this question," Kim added. This work was described in a study published Oct. 22 in the journal Scientific Reports.

item.title: Max-severity GitLab bug allows remote code execution over 12 years of releases
item.description: GitLab on Wednesday patched a maximum-severity flaw that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on self-managed servers under certain conditions. Affected software releases date back a full 12 years - so upgrade to a fixed version now. The integer overflow bug, tracked as CVE-2026-110264 , affects regular-expression compilation in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), including versions dating back to GitLab 7.0, released in June 2014. The flaw, “under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server due to integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression,” the vendor said in its release notes. GitLab released fixes in versions 19.5.1, 19.4.3, and 19.3.6, and backported the patch to versions 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, and 18.11.13. The vendor “strongly recommends” that all organizations running vulnerable software upgrade to a fixed version “as soon as possible.” GitLab-managed infrastructure, including GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, remains patched, and the vendor also released two threat detections ( here and here ) for customers with self-managed instances. Bug hunter Johan Carlsson reported the vulnerability through GitLab’s HackerOne bug bounty program. “For organizations running self-managed GitLab infrastructure, the potential impact is severe,” warned threat-detection firm SOC Prime. “GitLab repositories frequently contain source code, CI/CD configuration, deployment secrets, access tokens, infrastructure definitions, and connections to production environments. Server-level compromise could therefore create opportunities for credential theft, repository manipulation, supply chain attacks, persistence, or lateral movement.” While there’s no indication - yet - of any in-the-wild exploitation attempts, we’d expect criminals to start scanning for vulnerable instances soon. The ongoing PHP chaos may have given defenders a short head-start on this one, but considering the perfect 10 CVSS severity rating and GitLab’s reach into the enterprise - it claims 50 million registered users and more than 50 percent of the Fortune 100 - that’s not going to last long. Last month, attackers started battering another max-severity flaw in the same GitLab CE and EE products just days after the vendor issued a patch, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and private researchers.®

item.title: Fifa increases preparation money for Women’s World Cup to match men’s teams
item.description: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026 Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each. In 2023, the total preparation money for the tournament was $31m; it will now be $80m. Continue reading...

item.title: Scientists turned art detectives date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual night sky in 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's known location and other factors, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon didn't line up.

item.title: Meta shocked by $25B fine after N.M. refused to join multistate settlement
item.description: Meta must pay $25 billion to New Mexico after a jury found the tech giant guilty of nearly 44 million violations of state consumer protection laws. The largest fine to ever hit Meta came after New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez declined to join an $18 billion settlement Meta reached earlier this year with attorneys general in nearly all states. In his opinion Wednesday, US district court judge Francis J. Mathew said there was no “bright line rule” for determining the appropriate penalty for Meta's repeated and willful deception of users since 2010 about their “control of data, third-party data misuse, misinformation, hate speech, and equal enforcement.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...
