item.content:encoded:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn . "I feel enormous pride in what we accomplished together, and real sadness that this journey has come to an end." For the mission team, the farewell capped a decade of high-stakes engineering, on-the-fly troubleshooting and nail-biting close calls that ultimately delivered to Earth the largest asteroid sample ever collected in space, one that held secrets from the early solar system . Long before launch, the team faced obstacles that nearly thwarted the endeavor — chiefly, two rejections from NASA — before finally securing the green light for the $1 billion project under the New Frontiers Program in 2011. When OSIRIS-REx launched on Sept. 8, 2016, on a two-year journey across the inner solar system, Bennu was little more than a point of light in telescopes. Scientists expected the asteroid’s surface to be a smooth, sandy sphere where OSIRIS-REx could seamlessly touch down. Much to their surprise, however, when the probe arrived at the asteroid in late 2018, it revealed Bennu to be a treacherous, loosely bound amalgamation of jagged boulders. "Our expectations about the asteroid's surface were completely wrong," Lauretta said in an Oct. 7 statement from the University of Arizona. "There was no obvious place to collect a sample anywhere." When OSIRIS-REx touched down on a small crater named Nightingale , Bennu offered so little structural resistance that scientists said its surface reacted more like fluid than a hard, rocky shell. The spacecraft's sampling head sank directly into the asteroid, stopping after burrowing 20 inches (51 centimeters) deep by firing its thrusters at the right time to pull away, with the precious sample in hand. NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft captured this series of images of asteroid Bennu on April 14, 2020, during the first rehearsal of the mission's sample collection event. The actual sample retrieval was extremely close to the way this looks. (Image credit: NASA/Goddard/University of Arizona) Then came another nail-biting moment: The sample collector lid got jammed in a partially open position because so much material was scooped up, allowing fragments of the precious cargo to escape. In a race against time to prevent further loss, the mission team quickly stowed the sampler head directly inside the return capsule, securing the cosmic treasure for its journey back to Earth. Even the final return to Earth , on Sept. 24, 2023, kept the team on edge: A parachute failed to deploy properly during reentry, forcing a tense but ultimately safe landing in the Utah desert. "Successful exploration missions are not those that avoid surprises; they are those that are deliberately designed to adapt to them," Lauretta said in the statement, quoting a line from the mission's final report to NASA. "That certainly describes OSIRIS-REx," he said. "Again and again, the mission presented us with circumstances we had not expected, and again and again, this team found a way forward." The mission's triumphs began long before the samples reached Earth. For example, the probe set a Guinness World Record when it slid into orbit around the 1,610-foot-wide (490 meters) Bennu, which became the smallest object ever circled by a spacecraft. The scientific payoff that followed included remote-sensing work that confirmed Bennu's surface is coated in carbon-bearing compounds . Those observations also revealed that Bennu was once part of a much larger, water-rich parent asteroid that shattered in a catastrophic collision in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The returned sample — which weighs 4.29 ounces (121.6 grams) here on Earth, more than twice the mission's requirement — continues to thrill and occupy scientists. A wave of research papers, now topping 200, continues to piece together the composition and history of the ancient space rock. Among other findings, Bennu's pristine material has revealed amino acids and sugars that, on Earth, are essential for life , alongside a history of exposure to liquid water that could have served as the "broth" for these compounds to interact. More discoveries are likely to come. Most of the returned Bennu sample is being preserved for future generations of scientists, who will study it "with questions and instruments we cannot yet anticipate," Lauretta said in the statement. Though its OSIRIS-REx chapter is closed, the spacecraft itself is far from retired. Renamed OSIRIS-APEX (OSIRIS-APophis EXplorer), the probe is using its remaining propellant to head toward Apophis , another near-Earth asteroid and a different type of space rock from Bennu. It is scheduled to arrive in 2029.

item.title: Sophie Okonedo Is Serving Major Fashion Moments on the Clarissa Press Tour | See Photos
item.description: @nellkalonji From feather-trimmed Dior to fringe, the British-Nigerian actress is making a case for fashion that feels as good as it looks. Sophie Okonedo has always been one to watch on the red carpet and the Academy Award nominee has a knack for choosing looks that feel quietly dramatic. Her latest press tour for Clarissa is no exception. From sweeping feathers and playful fringe to intricate embellishments, Okonedo has been embracing pieces that bring movement and dimension to streamlined silhouettes. Ahead, we’re taking a closer look at some standout moments from her Clarissa press tour thus far. @nellkalonji Feathered Drama at Cannes For the film’s Cannes Film Festival premiere, Okonedo wore a custom black Dior gown. The dress featured an asymmetric neckline framed by delicate black feathers, which continued around the skirt and into the sweeping train. The feather detailing is part of the gown’s architecture, adding softness and movement to its otherwise structured shape. Okonedo also switched up her cornrows for a new hair color and style, giving the look an unexpected beauty twist. @nellkalonji Old Hollywood Glamour With a Modern Twist At the Magnum Cannes After Party she made a compelling case for this wonderful buttery champagne hue, stepping out in a figure-skimming satin gown paired with a lush faux-fur stole. There’s something wonderfully old Hollywood about this look, but Okonedo gives it a distinctly modern sensibility. The softly structured neckline and fluid silhouette lend the dress an understated elegance, while the plush stole introduces an unexpected contrast that makes the entire ensemble feel considerably more interesting. Her sculptural curls are another highlight, bringing an almost playful quality to an otherwise sophisticated look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Fringe Benefits at the BAFTA Tea Party At Sunday’s BAFTA Tea Party Q&A as part of the New York Film Festival celebrations, Okonedo returned to her signature cornrows and leaned into another texture-heavy moment, this time in a halter-neck dress from Luar’s Fall 2026 collection. The elongated silhouette was deceptively simple, allowing the details to take center stage. Slashed embellishments and cascading fringe created plenty of movement without overwhelming the look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Paired with Jimmy Choo Ixia pumps, the silhouette remained sleek, but the interplay of cutouts and fringe gave the ensemble a slightly rebellious edge. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde A Lesson in Tactile Dressing From Chanel For a press junket in Midtown Manhattan, Okonedo stepped out in a textured white look from Chanel ’s Fall 2026 collection, and it might be her most daring outfit of the tour so far. At first glance, the silhouette was relatively straightforward. Look closer, though, and the intricate surface detailing completely grabs you, gradually intensifying toward the hem. Okonedo finished the look with a crocodile-effect Chanel clutch and oversized sunglas

The elongated silhouette was deceptively simple, allowing the details to take center stage. Slashed embellishments and cascading fringe created plenty of movement without overwhelming the look. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde Paired with Jimmy Choo Ixia pumps, the silhouette remained sleek, but the interplay of cutouts and fringe gave the ensemble a slightly rebellious edge. @nellkalonji via @thehapablonde A Lesson in Tactile Dressing From Chanel For a press junket in Midtown Manhattan, Okonedo stepped out in a textured white look from Chanel ’s Fall 2026 collection, and it might be her most daring outfit of the tour so far. At first glance, the silhouette was relatively straightforward. Look closer, though, and the intricate surface detailing completely grabs you, gradually intensifying toward the hem. Okonedo finished the look with a crocodile-effect Chanel clutch and oversized sunglasses, giving an otherwise polished ensemble a playful, almost eccentric finish. The NYFF Beauty Look View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nick Barose (@nickbarose) For Okonedo’s New York Film Festival appearance, makeup artist Nick Barose leaned into a beauty look he described as “flirty fringes with joyous red lips.” For the complexion, Barose used Lisa Eldridge’s Seamless Skin Foundation in shade 22 and the new Luminist Concealer in shade 21 to create an even, natural-looking base. He added warmth and a fresh flush with the Velatura Balm Dewy Lip and Cheek Stick in Pomegranate Glace, while Elevated Glow Balm Concentrate in High-key Light brought a subtle radiance to the skin. Barose used the Seamless Glide Eye Pencil in Black Treacle alongside shades from the Eyeshadow Palette in Vega, adding a touch of Liquid Lurex Eyeshadow in Selene for dimension. Kitten Lash Mascara gave the lashes a fluttery finish and the new Kitten Brow Fluffy Hold and Flyaway Gel kept the brows polished. Barose paired Enhance and Define Lip Pencil in Duchess with Rouge Experience lipstick in Ribbon for a rich, vibrant red that brought instant energy to the look. It’s a beauty combination that feels especially right for Okonedo. The complexion is fresh, the eyes have just enough definition and the lipstick delivers the drama. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nell Kalonji (@nellkalonji) A Golden Moment Courtesy of Prada at the BFI London Film Festival Sophie Okonedo attended the Clarissa premiere at Vue West End during the BFI London Film Festival , wearing a yellow satin Prada gown that had all the makings of a standout red carpet moment. Okonedo naturally gravitates towards unexpected details and pieces that might overwhelm someone else but somehow feel entirely natural on her. The colour is stunning against her skin, while the twisted neckline and open back, finished with a delicate bow, offer exactly the kind of thoughtful design details we love to see. From behind, it’s practically a different dress. Another stunning look from the British-Nigerian star. item.title: Googlebook review: Google’s new laptops are woefully underbaked
item.description: Great hardware let down by software flaws on these pricey machines that combine ChromeOS with Android Google’s attempt to create a new type of laptop to compete with Windows and macOS machines is finally here, combining the best of ChromeOS and Android into the new Googlebook. With advanced links to Android phones and the best of Google built in, can these Googlebooks really compete with a MacBook Air or Surface Laptop? I took two for a spin to find out. For years, Chromebooks have been the boss of budget laptops, but Googlebooks take a different, far more premium approach. Made by a range of traditional PC makers, including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo, they start at £999 (€1,099/ $899 / A$2,299 ) – a far cry from the £160 Chromebooks. Continue reading...

item.title: New 'Blade Runner 2099' trailer is a space fan's dream with sinister starships and strange exoplanets (video)
item.description: null Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here! Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049." Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, " Blade Runner 2099" 's plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers. This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm. Check it out below: It’s executive produced by showrunner Silka Louisa ("Shining Girls”) and stars Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh ("Everything Everywhere All at Once") as Olwen, playing a fading replicant Blade Runner who joins forces with Hunter Schafer’s ("Euphoria") Cora, a pure human on the run attempting to evade a squad of exterminating Blade Runners while examining their existential natures. But aside from the dazzling visuals of the City of Angels at the gates of the 22nd century, fans will also be strapping in for some cool outer space action, as evidenced by fresh footage delivering some arresting scenes of space travel, off-world planets, and Yeoh in a bizarre helmet. "Blade Runner 2099" hits Prime Video starting on Nov. 25, 2026 (Image credit: Prime Video) " Blade Runner 2099" 's cast includes Dimitri Abold ("The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes") and Lewis Gribben ("Somewhere Boy”) alongside Katelyn Rose Downey ("The Nun II"), Daniel Rigby ('Renegade Nell"), Johnny Harris ("A Gentleman in Moscow"), Amy Lennox ("Only Child"), Sheila Atim ("The Woman King") and Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon”). Launching with an 8-episode debut season and executive produced by Scott Free Productions, "Blade Runner 2099" and its new world order lands on Prime Video on Nov. 25, 2026.

item.title: The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia
item.description: null Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set. This 1478 piece set is essentially two dioramas crammed into a single display piece. The top of the model depicts a spinning UFO floating above one of those iconic coniferous forests that dominated 90s sci-fi. Why? Because — thanks to some generous tax credits — it was cheaper to shoot in Vancouver, so that's where they all flocked. Disney Plus / Hulu bundle: was $12.99 now $11.99 Catch Mulder and Scully in every season of The X-Files on Hulu, which is available bundled with Disney+ for only $11.99/month for the first six months, then increasing to $12.99/month. View Deal Mulder and Scully closing in on our "Grey" alien friend in the woods. (Image credit: Future (Ian Stokes)) Beneath the woodland scene, though, is the real star of the show: Mulder's office, squirrelled away in the basement of the FBI's J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. This dingy little office is where Scully meets "Spooky Mulder", kicking off a glorious sci-fi odyssey that would last for eleven seasons (and two movies). Mulder's dingy little base of operations has been stunningly recreated here, with both overt references and subtle nods that X-Files fans will appreciate. The iconic "I want to believe" poster adorns the wall, alongside photographs of crop circles and a newspaper clipping from a paper called "The Lone Brickman" — a nice nod to " The Lone Gunmen ". There's even an actual X-File sitting on the desk, and a cute Lego spoof of the "Face on Mars", with a photo on the wall that shows a Lego head on the moon. The X-Files Complete Boxset: $160 Prefer to actually own your media? Make your way through this X-Files Complete Boxset on DVD. Just bear in mind that you will need a region-free DVD player to watch it with. The iconic "I Want To Believe" poster. Future (Ian Stokes) Newspaper clippings were a staple of the X-Files office. Future (Ian Stokes) The show's legendary tagline is proudly displayed on the front. Future (Ian Stokes) X(Files) marks the spot. Future (Ian Stokes) It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. Future (Ian Stokes) It's been a hot minute since I watched The X-Files (that DVD box set beside my TV is calling to me), but even so, I had a blast building my way down memory lane, remembering episodes as I assembled the diorama. I love the little touches, like the display cabinets filled with artifacts, the VHS tapes scattered around the office and the black oil spillage on the floor. As with most Lego sets, the minifigures are half the joy. You get Mulder and Scully, obviously, with the dynamic duo of FBI agents both rocking flashlights (no smartphones with built-in lights back in the 90s). Mulder is wearing dark blue, while Scully is rocking an orangey brown suit, with both of them sporting an FBI badge. Outside of the principal pair, you also get Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man. Mulder's partner-turned-nemesis Alex Krycek also gets a suitably devious-looking minifig. It's the gloves, they just make him look like a bad man (which, to be fair, he is). Finally, to ramp up the paranormal scale, we also get a pair of monster minifigs: a grey alien and Flukeman minifigures. The grey alien was a must-have, especially given the UFO floating atop this display piece, but the one-off monster of the week, Flukeman, felt like a weird choice. Agents Mulder and Scully, FBI. Future (Ian Stokes) Assistant Director Skinner, Mr X, and the Cigarette Smoking Man in Mulder's Office. Future (Ian Stokes) Also, this John Doggett erasure will not stand. Sure, he could never replace Mulder, but Robert Patrick's seasons eight and nine run was excellent and he deserved a spot here. And while I'm voicing minor gripes, the usual Lego FOMO tricks were in force with this set; if you pre-ordered, you got an exclusive gift set — Scully's Lab — free of charge. This extra little diorama isn't necessary, but it does feel like the collection is incomplete without it and it's not for sale separately, so you'll have to try your luck with eBay scalpers if you want it. Speaking of Scully, Gillian Anderson has stated that after season 11 wrapped in 2018, she was done with the role. That wasn't entirely accurate, though, as she donned the lab gloves one more time for the Lego X-Files set advert . It's a short bit of fan service, but a nice touch, and, once again, it sparks those 90s neurons. All these delicious Member Berries come at a price, though, and that's the price. This blast from the past will set you back $199 (£179 in the UK). That's no small chunk of change. But then again, anyone who wants this set is in their thirties or forties and can probably afford that outlay for the nostalgia trip. And look at it this way: when The X-Files debuted back in 1993, the price would only have been about $86. I had a great time building the Lego X-Files set and if you're a fan of the series, you will too. Nostalgia often feels like a cheat code to our hearts, but there's nothing wrong with that. We deserve to remember the good times and the truth is that The X-Files was about as good as it ever got for sci-fi fans. You can buy the Lego X-Files set now, available for $199/£179 from the Lego store.

item.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
item.description: null Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system . a rocket launches into a night sky from a seaside pad (Image credit: JAXA) It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. item.content:encoded: null Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos. If everything goes according to plan, MMX will become the first spacecraft to land on and return samples from Phobos for study back on Earth, which scientists think could shed light on a decades-old mystery about the moons' origins and reveal clues about the formation of the early solar system . a rocket launches into a night sky from a seaside pad (Image credit: JAXA) It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket, which was jointly developed by JAXA and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. After clearing its launch pad today, the 207-foot-tall (63 meters) launch vehicle flew a nominal trajectory through its ascent corridor over the Pacific Ocean, jettisoning its four solid boosters in pairs just before the flight clock reached two minutes. The rocket shed its payload fairings about one minute and 20 seconds later, exposing MMX to the vacuum of space for the first time. H3's first stage, powered by two LE-9 rocket engines, channels a mixture of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen to produce a combined thrust of 331,000 pounds (1,471 kN), according to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. As the mission clock approached T+5 minutes, H3 executed its main engine cutoff procedure and separated from the second stage, which ignited its engines for a 5.5-minute burn about 10 seconds later. All continued to go to plan after that. The H3's upper stage ignited its engine for a second time for a trans-Mars injection burn about one hour and four minutes after liftoff, a maneuver that lasted roughly six minutes and 25 seconds and took MMX to a maximum velocity of about 24,145 mph (38,858 kph). MMX was released from the rocket's upper stage right on schedule, about one minute after the completion of that burn and roughly 71 minutes after liftoff. The success elicited loud cheers in mission control, which viewers saw and heard on JAXA's launch webcast. MMX is now under its own power, and on course for Mars. The interplanetary transit will last about 10 months, with the spacecraft scheduled to arrive at the Red Planet in August 2027. When it does, MMX's propulsion module will execute an orbital insertion burn to place itself in a quasi-satellite orbit (QSO) around Phobos, which places MMX within the space around the moon as both circle Mars. MMX will spend about three years in the Martian system, devoting much of that time to studying the 14-mile-wide (22 km) Phobos with its science instruments. The spacecraft also carries the IDEFIX rover, a joint effort of the space agencies of France and Germany, which is scheduled to deploy to the surface of Phobos in late 2028 or early 2029. After a mapping campaign to select suitable landing sites, MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule. Following its second landing and sample collection, MMX will briefly return to QSO with Phobos before transferring to a more elongated orbit around Mars that intersects with the planet's smaller moon, Deimos, which is just 8 miles (14 km) in diameter. During the last several months of its time around Mars, MMX will perform a series of Deimos flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031. Scientists are counting on those samples, and other data collected during MMX's time around Mars, to answer a decades-old question surrounding the Martian moons' origins. Competing theories and conflicting evidence point to two possibilities for how Mars got its moons . Their near-circular, equatorial orbits suggest a narrative similar to how Earth's moon is thought to have formed — as a result of a massive planetary impact between Mars and some other giant space rock, which broke off pieces of the planet that eventually coalesced to form the natural satellites that orbit there today. A composite image with Mars and its two moons, Phobos and Deimos. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona) Neither Phobos nor Deimos is spherical, isntead; both are oblong and lumpy, like potatoes. That fact — along with their chemical composition, as far as we have been able to tell using telescopic spectroscopy — point to the possibility that Phobos and Deimos were asteroids from the early solar system that were captured by Mars' gravitational pull. Figuring out the moons' true origin story would provide key clues about Mars' geological past, the solar system's early history and the formation of the inner planets , mission team members have said. Once the MMX samples are safely returned to Earth, scientists will study their composition and mineralogy, then compare such chemical fingerprints with those of Martian rocks and asteroid material. These analyses, combined with data collected by MMX during its mission, will help nail down the origin of Phobos — and by extension, Deimos. — by While JAXA leads MMX, the mission is an international effort, with interagency partnerships between JAXA, NASA and the European Space Agency (ESA), as well as U.S. and European companies, which supplied a handful of the spacecraft's scientific hardware and communications equipment. NASA's contributions to MMX include the Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma rays and Neutrons (MEGANE, pronounced "meh-gah-nay") device, which is a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer built by the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL); a Honeybee Robotics-built pneumatic sampler; and communications support using the agency's Deep Space Network. NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission, which includes funding for United States scientists and astromaterials experts on the MMX team. The agency is getting something concrete for such contributions: At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study. Those materials will be transferred and maintained at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston for analysis and long-term preservation. MMX is not the first Phobos sample-return project to take flight, by the way. That distinction goes to Russia's Phobos-Grunt ("Phobos-Soil") mission, which launched in November 2011 but failed to get out of Earth orbit due to a rocket glitch. The 14.5-ton spacecraft eventually crashed back to Earth over the Pacific Ocean in January 2012. Editor's note: This story was updated at 5 p.m. ET on Oct. 19 with news of MMX's successful separation from the H3 rocket's upper stage.

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars
item.description: null On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity. Artist’s illustration showing the separation of the ExoMars 2016 entry, descent and landing demonstrator module, named Schiaparelli, from the Trace Gas Orbiter, and heading for Mars. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered ExoMars 2016 was a landmark mission for the European Space Agency and designed to be the vanguard of a two-flight ExoMars program to send an orbiter, lander and rover to Mars. Launched in March 2016, ExoMars 2016 aimed to achieve two goals for ESA and Russia. First, the mission aimed to use the Schiaparelli lander to test landing techniques that would be vital on a planned ExoMars 2018 rover . Second, the mission would deliver a critical orbiter around Mars to study the planet's atmosphere and serve as a communications link for that future Mars rover. In the end, ExoMars 2016 was just a partial success, with ESA officials calling it "96% successful." due to the loss of the lander. While Schiaparelli separated smoothly from the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter spacecraft, it stopped communicating with Earth just 1 minute before its planned landing on Oct. 19. Photos from NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter at Mars later revealed what appeared to be its crash site and, nearby, its jettisoned parachute. Officials suspect Schiaparelli did not fire its descent thrusters as designed in order to slow itself enough for a safe landing. A data glitch was cited as its cause . The Trace Gas Orbiter, meanwhile, continues to study Mars to this day and has spent 10 years and counting studying the Martian atmosphere . The launch of ExoMars 2018, which includes the Mars rover Rosalind Franklin, was delayed by the Schiaparelli failure, as well as the loss of its Russian Proton rocket when ESA severed its partnership with Russia over that country's war on Ukraine. The ExoMars rover is now expected to launch no earlier than 2028, with a landing on Mars expected in 2030. In 2026, another country took aim at Mars on this day. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency attempted to launch the ambitious Martian Moons eXploration mission (called MMX) to land a probe on the Mars moon Phobos and return samples to Earth. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
item.description: null The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface. This helped them to figure out how much the moon has contracted over time, and they now estimate that the moon's radius has decreased by about 148 feet (45 meters) over the past 400 to 800 million years. "The number of these young faults revealed in LROC images is much greater than I ever imagined," study lead Thomas Watters, a geologist and scientist emeritus at the Center for Earth and Planetary Studies at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum, said in a statement . "As the interior of the moon continues to cool and contract, it is expected that the growth of existing faults and formation of new faults continues today." Lobate scarps on the lunar surface, as seen by LROC. (Image credit: NASA/KARI/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian ) With these LROC observations, researchers in this study saw a variety of different types of cracks and landforms across the lunar surface. This included lobate scarps, or long, curved structures that form when the moon's surface contracts, cracks and is pushed upwards; and small mare ridges, or narrow "wrinkles" in the lunar surface, across the dark plains on the moon . Lobate scarps on the moon, as seen by LROC. (Image credit: NASA/KARI/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian) Tectonic activity on the moon looks a lot different than it does on Earth. On our own planet, there are about 15 major tectonic plates. On the moon, there are no tectonic plates at all. Instead, the moon has a single-plate body meaning its outer shell is a single piece only broken by faults or other such cracks created by the moon contracting. This means that instead of faults or cracks appearing at tectonic plate boundaries, they are instead scattered all over the moon. A global map of lunar faults. Red lines indicate over 8,900 lobate scarps while blue lines show over 2,000 small mare ridges. (Image credit: NASA/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian) By mapping these thousands of different features, all created from the moon cooling and contracting over time, the researchers are piecing together lunar history. (Image credit: NASA/KARI/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian ) With these LROC observations, researchers in this study saw a variety of different types of cracks and landforms across the lunar surface. This included lobate scarps, or long, curved structures that form when the moon's surface contracts, cracks and is pushed upwards; and small mare ridges, or narrow "wrinkles" in the lunar surface, across the dark plains on the moon . Lobate scarps on the moon, as seen by LROC. (Image credit: NASA/KARI/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian) Tectonic activity on the moon looks a lot different than it does on Earth. On our own planet, there are about 15 major tectonic plates. On the moon, there are no tectonic plates at all. This means that instead of faults or cracks appearing at tectonic plate boundaries, they are instead scattered all over the moon. A global map of lunar faults. Red lines indicate over 8,900 lobate scarps while blue lines show over 2,000 small mare ridges. (Image credit: NASA/ASU/Intuitive Machines/Smithsonian) By mapping these thousands of different features, all created from the moon cooling and contracting over time, the researchers are piecing together lunar history. In addition to finding the extent to which the moon has shrunk over time, they also found that some areas of the moon are covered in many more faults than other areas, and the areas with fewer cracks and faults have thicker moon crust. This led them to conclude that not only are these areas with thicker crust more stable, but they suggest that a great deal of the widespread cracks in the lunar surface were created later in the moon's history as, in its earlier years, its thick crust would have insulated the moon's warm interior and prevented cooling, contracting and cracking. This work was described in a study published Oct. 14 in The Planetary Science Journal.

item.title: Kikelomo Atanda-Owo Celebrates 20 Years in Media Unveils Podcast With Husband Reuben Abati
item.description: Ace broadcaster, media entrepreneur and host of Real Talk With Kike , Kikelomo Atanda-Owo , alongside her husband, veteran journalist and broadcaster Dr. Reuben Abati , has officially unveiled “ The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast ,” marking an exciting new chapter in their broadcasting careers. The announcement was made on Saturday, October 10, 2026, during the celebration of Kikelomo Atanda-Owo’s 20 years in the media industry, held at Eko Hotels & Suites, Lagos. The occasion also commemorated the seventh anniversary of her flagship talk show, Real Talk With Kike, bringing together distinguished personalities, media executives, business leaders, industry stakeholders and well-wishers. The unveiling of The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast represents a significant milestone for the celebrated media couple, who are bringing their wealth of experience, individual perspectives and shared passion for meaningful conversations to a new digital platform. The podcast is envisioned as a platform for engaging, thought-provoking and insightful conversations on issues shaping contemporary society, including governance, politics, relationships, family, culture, lifestyle, entertainment and everyday experiences. According to Lagos News Hub, combining Dr. Reuben Abati’s extensive background in journalism, political analysis and public affairs with Kikelomo Atanda-Owo’s distinctive approach to human-interest storytelling, lifestyle conversations and audience engagement, the podcast promises a compelling blend of perspectives, experience and authenticity. Beyond their individual accomplishments in broadcasting, the new podcast creates an opportunity for the couple to explore important subjects together, bringing their different professional experiences and viewpoints into conversations designed to inform, educate and entertain audiences. For Kikelomo Atanda-Owo, the unveiling comes at a particularly significant moment in her career as she celebrates two decades of consistency, resilience and impact in the Nigerian media landscape. Over the years, she has established herself as a respected voice in broadcasting, using Real Talk With Kike to facilitate conversations around personal development, relationships, social issues, leadership and the experiences that shape everyday life. Dr. Reuben Abati, on his part, brings decades of experience as a journalist, columnist, public affairs commentator and former presidential spokesperson. His contributions to political discourse and national conversations have established him as one of Nigeria’s recognisable media voices. Together, the couple will seek to create a distinctive podcast experience that combines serious conversations with relatable discussions, personal insights and engaging exchanges. BellaNaija is a Media Partner for The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast The post Kikelomo Atanda-Owo Celebrates 20 Years in Media Unveils Podcast With Husband Reuben Abati appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Kikelomo Atanda-Owo Celebrates 20 Years in Media: Unveils Podcast With Reuben Abati as Abike Dabiri Other Dignitaries Attend
item.description: It was a celebration of excellence, resilience, innovation and over two decades of remarkable contributions to the Nigerian media industry as ace broadcaster and media entrepreneur, Kikelomo Atanda-Owo , celebrated her 20th anniversary in broadcasting alongside the seventh anniversary of her flagship television programme, Real Talk With Kike , at Eko Hotels & Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Saturday, October 10, 2026. The high-profile event, themed “The Future of Nigeria: Where Leadership, Innovation, Culture & Media Converge to Shape Nation Building,” brought together prominent personalities from government, business, media, entertainment and the diplomatic community to celebrate the broadcaster’s professional journey and examine the role of leadership, innovation and responsible media in Nigeria’s development. One of the major highlights of the occasion was the official unveiling of “The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast ,” a new digital media platform jointly introduced by Kikelomo Atanda-Owo and her husband, veteran journalist, political analyst and former presidential spokesperson, Dr. Reuben Abati. The anniversary celebration also featured a keynote address delivered by the Secretary to the Lagos State Government, Barrister Bimbola Salu-Hundeyin , who represented the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat . The keynote session reflected the conference’s central theme, drawing attention to the intersection of leadership, innovation, culture and the media in shaping Nigeria’s future. The occasion also provided an opportunity to reflect on the responsibilities of media practitioners in promoting constructive national conversations and encouraging greater participation in nation-building. The event, according to Lagos News Hub attracted an impressive gathering of distinguished personalities, including Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM) ; Hannatu Musa Musawa , Honourable Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy; Dr. Allen Onyema , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace ; Tosin Akerele ; and Kola Adesina , Group Managing Director of Sahara Power Group, alongside other notable personalities from the public and private sectors. Their presence underscored the significance of the occasion and the relationships Kikelomo Atanda-Owo has cultivated throughout her two-decade career in the media industry. Beyond the celebration of professional milestones, the gathering created an avenue for networking, meaningful engagement and conversations around the evolving Nigerian media landscape, particularly the growing influence of digital platforms, content innovation and strategic storytelling. item.content:encoded: It was a celebration of excellence, resilience, innovation and over two decades of remarkable contributions to the Nigerian media industry as ace broadcaster and media entrepreneur, Kikelomo Atanda-Owo , celebrated her 20th anniversary in broadcasting alongside the seventh anniversary of her flagship television programme, Real Talk With Kike , at Eko Hotels & Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Saturday, October 10, 2026. The high-profile event, themed “The Future of Nigeria: Where Leadership, Innovation, Culture & Media Converge to Shape Nation Building,” brought together prominent personalities from government, business, media, entertainment and the diplomatic community to celebrate the broadcaster’s professional journey and examine the role of leadership, innovation and responsible media in Nigeria’s development. One of the major highlights of the occasion was the official unveiling of “The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast ,” a new digital media platform jointly introduced by Kikelomo Atanda-Owo and her husband, veteran journalist, political analyst and former presidential spokesperson, Dr. Reuben Abati. The anniversary celebration also featured a keynote address delivered by the Secretary to the Lagos State Government, Barrister Bimbola Salu-Hundeyin , who represented the Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat . The keynote session reflected the conference’s central theme, drawing attention to the intersection of leadership, innovation, culture and the media in shaping Nigeria’s future. The occasion also provided an opportunity to reflect on the responsibilities of media practitioners in promoting constructive national conversations and encouraging greater participation in nation-building. The event, according to Lagos News Hub attracted an impressive gathering of distinguished personalities, including Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM) ; Hannatu Musa Musawa , Honourable Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy; Dr. Allen Onyema , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Air Peace ; Tosin Akerele ; and Kola Adesina , Group Managing Director of Sahara Power Group, alongside other notable personalities from the public and private sectors. Their presence underscored the significance of the occasion and the relationships Kikelomo Atanda-Owo has cultivated throughout her two-decade career in the media industry. Beyond the celebration of professional milestones, the gathering created an avenue for networking, meaningful engagement and conversations around the evolving Nigerian media landscape, particularly the growing influence of digital platforms, content innovation and strategic storytelling. For Kikelomo Atanda-Owo, the occasion was a celebration of consistency, determination, professional growth and the enduring relevance of meaningful conversations in a rapidly changing media environment. Through Real Talk With Kike, which has now completed seven years, she has continued to engage audiences on relationships, personal development, lifestyle, social challenges and other important subjects, establishing the programme as a platform for thought-provoking discussions. With the successful celebration of 20 years in media, seven years of Real Talk With Kike, and the unveiling of a new podcast alongside her husband, Kikelomo Atanda-Owo has opened another chapter in her career, reinforcing her commitment to storytelling, media innovation and conversations that contribute meaningfully to society. item.title: Saskay Celebrates Master’s Degree From VUB Brussels School of Governance in Hertunba | See Photos
item.description: Saskay celebrating her Master of Arts degree in Global Security and Strategy. Who says you need a suit to celebrate a master’s degree? Saskay is marking a major academic milestone on her own terms, swapping the Western-style outfit she originally planned for a look rooted in heritage. The Big Brother Naija star, whose real name is Tsakute Ladi Jonah , has earned a Master of Arts (MA) in Global Security and Strategy from VUB Brussels School of Governance, and her graduation photos make room for both her academic achievement and a conversation about how we dress for success. Reflecting on what the degree means to her, Saskay shared how studying a subject she has always been passionate about made the experience especially meaningful. Master of Arts (MA) in Global Security and Strategy. I got to study something I’ve always been passionate about, and that makes this degree mean so much more to me. I’ve poured so much of myself into this journey that my diploma is basically my baby. Saskay in the Hertunba Nola Kaftan for her graduation portraits. Her choice of outfit came about after her original plan fell through. Saskay had intended to wear a suit for the shoot, but her designer had an emergency and could not complete it in time. The change prompted her to reflect on why Western clothing is so often associated with academic achievement, and how graduation portraits can also celebrate cultural identity. I had a suit planned for this shoot, but my designer had an emergency and couldn’t get it ready in time. Things took a different turn, and it got me thinking about how we’ve come to associate education with western clothing. There’s something beautiful about celebrating an academic milestone in a way that also reflects who we are and where we come from. Saskay in her graduation outfit celebrating her MA in Global Security and Strategy. For the shoot, Saskay wore the Nola Kaftan by Hertunba, a flowing, 100% cotton design featuring motifs of palm trees, birds and dwellings. The motifs tell a metaphorical story of a small girl in a big village, with each illustration contributing to the larger narrative woven into the design. The kaftan featured a generous silhouette, fluid sleeves and an open drape, with its off-white and cream tones complemented by a chocolate brown silk veil. Saskay posing with her VUB Brussels School of Governance degree case. She paired the kaftan with traditional-inspired facial art, including a triangle on her forehead, a line across the bridge of her nose and a vertical line extending from her lower lip to her chin. Oversized leaf-shaped gold drop earrings, a layered beaded gold necklace, thick gold cuffs, wide bangles and statement rings completed her look. Beauty detail of Saskay featuring traditional African facial art markings, a shaved head, gold leaf earrings, and layered beaded jewellery for her Master’s degree graduation portraits. In some of the photographs, Saskay posed with a leather degree holder bearing her institutio

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
item.description: null Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets. "They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement . "Unlike exoplanets , free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are." Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light. "We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said. A forest (of brown dwarfs) Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory. To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius). Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold. Brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/NASA/JPL-Caltech) The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane. item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets. "They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement . "Unlike exoplanets , free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are." Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light. "We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said. A forest (of brown dwarfs) Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory. To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius). Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold. Brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/NASA/JPL-Caltech) The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane. "We’re seeing the signatures of these molecules and how they change from object to object across the entire temperature regime," said team member J. Davy Kirkpatrick, also of Caltech. "Our paper concentrated on just three dozen, but we have thousands more that we are in the process of analyzing. "I really want to see what bounds the universe places on the variety of brown dwarfs." All my colors Brown dwarfs have been routinely observed by other telescopes, including NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the agency's now-retired Spitzer Space Telescope , but the wide wavelength coverage of SPHEREx has made it particularly useful in observing these failed stars. That's good news for astronomers waiting for change in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs as they age and grow cold. The researchers found that some brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx are at a stage of extreme change in which their clouds are clearing, creating atmospheres rich in methane. The team may have discovered significant new details about brown dwarfs, but they are still on the proverbial mystery street when it comes to these strange celestial objects, "The state-of-the-art models are capturing the general chemical trend, but when it comes to these cloudy transitions, the models are struggling to match the data," said Rustamkulov. "No two brown dwarfs are alike. Even at the same temperature, their spectra look quite distinct." NASA’s SPHEREx reveals molecules like methane (CH4), carbon dioxide (CO2), and carbon monoxide (CO) in brown dwarf atmospheres. The telescope’s view of three different brown dwarfs appears on the left. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA, M.H. Wong (UC Berkeley) et al. Acknowledgments: M. Zamani) "This journey has turned many of us into accidental meteorologists. We know how hard it is to predict weather on our own planet, and we realize it's going to be just as challenging to explain the phenomena we see in these bizarre, cold objects," Kirkpatrick said. "The findings are a call to action to explore even more of these dark worlds." As astronomers resond to that call to action, I will ponder how I could have worked Bauhaus' Goth classic "Bela Lugosi is Dead" into this article. The team's research was published on Sept. 28 in The Astrophysical Journal.

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle Becomes Nigeria’s Youngest Female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at 40
item.description: Judicial portrait of Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN, partner at Afe Babalola & Co., who made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at the age of 40. Nigeria’s legal landscape has witnessed a momentous record as Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun – Adekunle joins the prestigious Inner Bar, officially becoming the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) in history. Attaining the highly coveted Silk rank at the age of 40, the seasoned advocate and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Nigeria has broken a long-standing ceiling, setting a inspiring milestone for women across the legal profession and beyond. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, MCIArb, is a distinguished partner at the renowned law firm Afe Babalola & Co. (Emmanuel Chambers). With a career spanning over 14 years of legal practice, she specialises in complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, strategic legal advisory, and international arbitration. Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN following her elevation as the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria. Her academic foundation includes a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) degree from Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. as a Partner in September 2013, her professional experience included key positions at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. Her historic elevation to Senior Advocate of Nigeria—a position reserved for legal practitioners who have distinguished themselves through exceptional skill, professional integrity, and significant contributions to Nigerian jurisprudence—marks a defining moment in contemporary law. Taking on the rank at 40 years old, she stands out as the youngest female lawyer to achieve this honour in Nigeria, carving a clear path for future generations of female lawyers to aim for the highest levels of leadership in the country’s judiciary and private bar. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). Her historic elevation to Senior Advocate of Nigeria—a position reserved for legal practitioners who have distinguished themselves through exceptional skill, professional integrity, and significant contributions to Nigerian jurisprudence—marks a defining moment in contemporary law. Taking on the rank at 40 years old, she stands out as the youngest female lawyer to achieve this honour in Nigeria, carving a clear path for future generations of female lawyers to aim for the highest levels of leadership in the country’s judiciary and private bar. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). item.title: Elephant Island is an icy sight from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 19, 2026
item.description: null Ice floats by in West Antarctica as winter comes to an end in the Southern Hemisphere. (Image credit: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space. What is it? Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica. Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic. In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean. It got its name both from the island's shape, which some liken to that of an elephant's head, and the fact that the island is home to a community of elephant seals. Why is it incredible? While a seal-inhabited island on the left floats near the Antarctic coast, across the water is a vast, frozen landscape. In just this snapshot, you can see about between 746 and 1,056 miles (1,200 to 1,700 kilometers) of the icy continent. This image was captured on Sept. 30, 2026. In the Southern Hemisphere, that was just past the end of winter. The absolute peak for sea ice in Antarctica fell just a couple weeks before, on Sept. 14, according to the National Snow and Ice Data Center, ESA reported . So in this one snapshot, we can see a near-maximum for sea ice in the Antarctic, spanning hundreds of miles. In observing our own planet from space, we are able to peer across vast landscapes, capturing important observational data. This is especially critical for the Antarctic as, with the progression of climate change , this sea ice continues to dwindle , adding to sea level rise among other serious consequences across the planet.

item.title: Nancy Isime, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere & More Star in Loving Itohan | Watch Trailer
item.description: Nancy Isime in traditional Edo wedding attire on the set of her debut executive producer film Loving Itohan. Remember when Nancy Isime announced she was stepping into the shoes of an executive producer for her very first feature film? Well, the moment is finally here, and we have our first real look at what she has been cooking up! The Nollywood favourite has unveiled the trailer for Loving Itohan , giving us a front-row seat to a drama packed with romance, secrets, and tough personal choices. The story centres on Itohan, a woman caught in a web of emotional conflict and hidden truths that threaten to turn her world upside down. As unexpected situations force her to make tough choices between her heart and her reality, she has to navigate what love truly demands when secrets begin to surface. Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe on set for Loving Itohan, in cinemas 6 November 2026. Sharing the trailer, Nancy Isime could not contain her excitement over bringing the story to life: It’s finally here! We’re excited to introduce you to our baby, Loving Itohan! After so much love, hard work, and dedication, we can finally share a little piece of this story with you. The official trailer is out, and we can’t wait for you to meet Itohan and fall in love with her story, just as we have. Directed by Orobosa Ikponmwen and produced by Emmanuel Izuoba alongside Nancy Isime as executive producer , the feature drama stars Nancy Isime in the lead role, alongside Uzor Arukwe , Martha Ehinome Orhiere , Dorathy Bachor , Chioma Nwosu , Obehi Aburime , and Grace Coker . Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe filming Loving Itohan. Nancy Isime on location with cast members filming scenes for Loving Itohan. For everyone looking forward to catching this one on the big screen, Loving Itohan arrives in cinemas nationwide on 6 November 2026. item.title: Nigerian Artists Who Have Sold Out London’s O2 Arena
item.description: The O2 Arena is one of the most popular music venues in the world. Its significance extends to Nigerian music. As Afrobeats was crossing over to the world, selling out London’s 02 Arena became one of the markers of that global expansion. Ayo Onikoyi , for Vanguard Newspaper , described the venue as “a symbol of global acceptance, a stamp of credibility, and a gateway to even greater success” for Nigerian artists. Filling a room with 1000 people requires a lot of work; now multiply that by 20, and imagine what how much effort it’d take to fill out a venue with 20, 000 people, screaming back your music at you. The London’s 02 Arena has a 20,000-seat capacity, and has become one of the most recognisable stages in Afrobeats’ international rise, offering artists an opportunity to perform before large audiences, connect with Nigerians and other African music lovers in the diaspora, and demonstrate the growing commercial appeal of Nigerian music. Its reputation as a venue for global superstars has also made performing there a significant career milestone. If you can sell out the 02 Arena, you could dare to sell out a bigger venue, stadiums, and many more, in the world. Being very popular in Nigeria does not translate to selling out venues like the O2 Arena; your music must have travelled far. Wizkid opened the 022 Arena door when he sold out the O2 Arena in 2018, becoming the first Nigerian artist to achieve the feat. Since then, Davido , Burna Boy , Asake and Rema have also taken their music to the celebrated London venue, with some returning for multiple shows. Here are the Nigerian artists who have sold out the O2 Arena: Wizkid Wizkid made history on 26 May 2018 when he sold out the O2 Arena with his Afrorepublik concert, becoming the first Nigerian artist to achieve the feat. The show featured appearances by other Nigerian and UK-based artists, including Tiwa Savage, Mr Eazi and many others. It marked a major moment for Afrobeats, demonstrating that Nigerian music could command a 20,000-capacity venue in London. He returned in 2021 during the Made in Lagos tour, when he sold out the iconic venues within minutes, and performed for three consecutive days. Davido On 27 January 2019, Davido headlined a sold-out show at the O2 Arena. The concert featured special appearances, including British actor Idris Elba and Jamaican artist Popcaan , and showcased Davido’s ability to bring his energetic performances and catalogue of hits to an international audience. The milestone further strengthened his position as one of Afrobeats’ leading global stars. Burna Boy Burna Boy sold out the O2 Arena on 27 August 2021 during his Spaceship tour. Asake After rising rapidly through the Nigerian music scene with hits, Asake took another major step in his career when he sold out the O2 Arena on 20 August 2023. Asake After rising rapidly through the Nigerian music scene with hits, Asake took another major step in his career when he sold out the O2 Arena on 20 August 2023. The show followed his successful sold-out performances at the smaller O2 Academy Brixton venue. He returned to the O2 Arena in 2024 for his Lungu Boy World Tour, reinforcing his growing international appeal and the reach of his distinctive street-pop sound, and returned again in 2026 during his In God We Trust tour. Rema Rema joined the list on 14 November 2023 when he sold out the O2 Arena. At just 23, he became one of the youngest Nigerian artists to headline a sold-out concert at the venue. The show featured an elaborate entrance, a live band and performances of songs from his growing catalogue, including his global hit “Calm Down.” It was a defining moment for the singer. Now, Olamide has announced his upcoming show at the O2 Arena in March 2027. The O2 Arena remains one of the most significant stages for Nigerian artists seeking to cement their place on the global music scene, and Olamide’s planned performance will be another important moment for Afrobeats. It will add his name to the growing list of Nigerian artists who have taken their music to the celebrated London venue, further demonstrating how far Nigerian music has travelled and how much further it can go. item.title: From a Casual Night Out to a Brand-New Car: How Queen Thompson Won Big in the Guinness ‘Open For More’ Promo!
item.description: When you head out for a night of good vibes with your friends, you expect great conversations, plenty of laughter, and maybe a few photos for the Gram. What you probably don’t expect is to walk away with the chance to win a brand-new car! That was the unexpected turn Queen Thompson ’s evening took when she became the grand prize winner of the recently concluded 10-week Guinness ‘Open For More’ promo. It started as a regular night out in Akwa Ibom. Queen and her friends had gone to one of their favourite spots to unwind, catch up and enjoy some chilled drinks. Among the bottles on the table was Guinness Foreign Extra Stout . At some point during the evening, Queen noticed the promo code beneath her bottle cap, brought out her phone, and entered it. Nothing elaborate, just a quick entry while enjoying the night. Little did she know that one simple entry would put her in the running for a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado worth ₦150 million! A few weeks later, Queen received a phone call from an official Guinness representative with news that would have anyone asking, “ Wait, what?! Is this for real? ” She had won the grand prize! But excitement wasn’t her first reaction. Having been defrauded twice earlier in the year, Queen was understandably cautious and initially wondered if the call was another scam. It took the official prize presentation for the news to fully sink in. At the handover ceremony at Guinness Nigeria’s headquarters in Ogba, Lagos, Queen’s win became official in the most memorable way. Girish Sharma , Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guinness Nigeria Plc , personally presented her with the keys to her brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado, as company executives, brand representatives, fellow prize winners and well-wishers gathered to celebrate the moment. Still taking it all in, Queen said, “I am still in shock! I never imagined that opening a bottle of Guinness Foreign Extra Stout would lead to me driving home in a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado. When I got the notification, I initially doubted it because I had been defrauded twice earlier this year. I am so grateful to Guinness for this incredible, life-changing gift. Truly, what God cannot do does not exist!” Now that’s one night out that ended with a plot twist nobody saw coming! The Guinness ‘Open For More’ promo may have wrapped up, but the winners’ stories remain memorable, especially the grand winner whose experience leaves us with a little reminder: stay open to possibilities; you never know when good news might be on the other end of a call. Queen’s story was the grand finale of a much bigger journey. Over 10 weeks, Guinness Nigeria rewarded 1,075 consumers across the country, with 1,000 people winning ₦100,000 each and another 75 becoming millionaires with ₦1 million apiece, before Queen drove home with the grand prize, a Toyota Land Cruiser Prado valued at ₦150 million. For Guinness, Open For More was a way to give something back to the consumers wh

item.title: Before They Say “I Do”, See Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Pre-Wedding Photos
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in an intimate pre-wedding portrait. Can you hear the wedding bells? Something beautiful is happening in Zlatan Ibile ’s world, and this time, it has nothing to do with a new song or music video. The Afrobeats star, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , is getting ready to celebrate his love for longtime partner Davita Omoniyi in a grand wedding ceremony on 24 October 2026. And while we’re still waiting to see what the couple have planned for their big day, their pre-wedding photographs are already giving us plenty to admire. From the gorgeous colour choices to the fashion and the sweet way they pose together, Zlatan and Davita are making the countdown to their wedding even more exciting. The couple have been together for years and share two children. Davita, a UK-based media personality and entrepreneur, reportedly took on the Omoniyi surname following their private civil registry ceremony earlier this year. Now, with their wedding celebration approaching, they’re preparing to mark another chapter of their relationship surrounded by family and friends. Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi posing together in pastel outfits for their official pre-wedding pictures. For their pre-wedding photographs, celebrity stylist Emmanuel Goodnews Icon brought together a lovely combination of pastel ice blue and blush pink against a rich teal studio backdrop. The colours worked beautifully together, with Davita’s gown and Zlatan’s tailored outfit offering two different takes on the same colour palette. Davita wore a strapless mermaid gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam, featuring micro-pleating and ruching across the bodice. The fitted silhouette opened into a voluminous bubble-hem train made from bubblegum pink taffeta, giving the dress an interesting contrast of structure and volume. She completed her look with a high braided ponytail, glowing makeup, a classic tennis necklace and matching diamond jewellery. Davita Omoniyi in a custom gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon. Beside her, Zlatan wore a bespoke light blue two-piece suit by T.I Nathan. His jacket featured a structured mandarin collar and concealed button placket, paired with relaxed wide-leg trousers. Dark wire-frame glasses and black patent leather shoes completed his look, keeping the styling simple while allowing the tailoring and colour to take centre stage. Zlatan Ibile styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon in a bespoke T.I Nathan suit The rich teal backdrop made the soft colours of their outfits even more striking, while their poses brought a lovely sense of closeness to the portraits. With 24 October just around the corner, the couple have given us a beautiful first look at their wedding style, and we’re curious to see what they’ll wear when the celebrations begin. Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi gearing up for their October 2026 wedding celebration. Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in their pre-wedding photoshoot ahead of their October 24 wedding cere
